findings.title: Runoff map: map_overlap normalizes lon and lat to [0,360), so domains that straddle 0° longitude or the equator take runoff from the whole latitude or longitude band
findings.what: generate_ESMF_map_via_xesmf(map_overlap=True) builds the destination bounding box from normalize_deg() of the node longitudes AND latitudes, then takes min/max. If the ocean domain crosses lon 0/360 (for example -5..5 or 355..365), the box becomes 0..~360 in longitude. If it crosses the equator, latitudes -5..5 become 0..5 plus 355..360, and the box becomes 0..~360 in latitude. In both cases no source cell is masked out. gen_rof_maps uses nearest_d2s, which sends every unmasked source cell to its nearest coastline cell, so the regional domain gets the runoff of every river in that band.
findings.trigger: Any CrocoDash case with active DROF/runoff (RunoffConfigurator.process -> mapping.gen_rof_maps) on a domain whose longitudes span 0°/360° in either convention, or whose latitudes span the equator. Examples: North Sea, Bay of Biscay, Gulf of Guinea, Amazon or Congo plumes, Galapagos.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/mom6_forge/r1_rof_overlap.py: synthetic global 2° rof mesh (all unmasked), a 10x10° ocean grid at 1° with a 3-column land strip, gen_rof_maps(). Expected about 30 source cells mapped, all inside the domain box. Observed: [east, 5..15E, 40..50N] 30 cells, lon 5..15 (correct); [pm, -5..5E] 900 cells, lon 1..359 (every longitude in the 40-50N band); [eq, 5..15E, -5..5N] 480 cells, lat -79..79 (every latitude). gen_rof_maps' conservation check still passes.
findings.root_cause: normalize_deg (mod 360) is applied to latitude, and plain min/max over normalized longitudes cannot describe an arc that crosses the 0/360 cut.
findings.smallest_fix: Compare latitudes raw. For longitude, use the circular window: the complement of the largest gap between sorted normalized node longitudes, then test mod(x - start, 360) <= width. The closed, unmerged mom6_forge PR #128 already implements this as _lon_window() and was never landed. Re-land it.

findings.title: get_mesh_dimensions swaps nx/ny on rotated grids (from_center angle around ±50-90°), which scrambles the runoff coastline mask, smoothing neighbours and Grid/Topo.from_esmf_mesh
findings.what: After getting nx correctly from element connectivity, get_mesh_dimensions swaps nx and ny whenever the first row of the mesh changes latitude more than longitude (mod 360). Rows of a rotated grid do exactly that. grid_from_esmf_mesh then reshapes centerCoords and elementMask as (nx, ny), so extract_coastline_mask runs on a scrambled 2D layout and flags interior ocean cells as coast. compute_smoothing_weights builds left/right/top/bottom from the wrong nx. reconstruct_from_esmf_mesh (Grid.from_esmf_mesh, Topo.from_esmf_mesh) returns a transposed, scrambled grid.
findings.trigger: Grid.from_center(..., angle_deg=60) (roughly |angle| in 50..90° at mid-latitudes) with nx != ny, then a CrocoDash case with active runoff (gen_rof_maps); or Grid.from_esmf_mesh / Topo.from_esmf_mesh on such a mesh.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/mom6_forge/r9_meshdims.py: from_center(30,-60,100e3,60e3,5e3,angle_deg=60) has true (nx,ny)=(20,12), but get_mesh_dimensions gives (12,20) and Grid.from_esmf_mesh gives shape (20,12) with wrong tlon. Angles 0 and 30 are correct. r11_coast.py: the coastline mask flags 128 cells, 108 of them not next to land (the real coast is 12 cells). r13_rot_rof.py: the angle-60 nn map sends runoff to 117 ocean cells, 105 of them not next to land.
findings.root_cause: An orientation heuristic based on lon/lat differences along the first row overrides the exact, connectivity-derived nx. Rows of rotated grids are not zonal.
findings.smallest_fix: Skip the swap for meshes written by mom6_forge, which are always row-major (to_esmf_mesh already writes the grid_topology attr; or write nx/ny attrs and prefer them). Keep the heuristic only for foreign meshes, and make it compare great-circle distances rather than raw lon/lat deltas.

findings.title: Topo.from_version_control reloads every bathymetry with min_depth=0.0, so cells shallower than the saved min_depth turn back into ocean
findings.what: from_version_control builds Topo(grid, 0.0, git=True). Its __init__ commits a new MinDepthEditCommand(new=0.0, old=0.0) to the history. reapply_changes replays it last, then tcm.undo() reverses that same command. Its old_value is 0.0, so min_depth stays 0.0 instead of going back to the stored value (the comment claiming otherwise is wrong). tmask, masked_depth, the written topog and the min_depth attr all change. Every load also adds two commits to the history.
findings.trigger: Saving a bathymetry with git=True (Topo(..., git=True) or TopoEditor) and reloading it with Topo.from_version_control(domain_dir), then using it in a CrocoDash Case.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/mom6_forge/r5_vc.py [plain]: Topo(min_depth=10, git=True), depth 500 m with row 0 at 5 m, one edit_depth. Original: min_depth=10.0, 18 ocean cells. Reloaded: min_depth=0.0, 24 ocean cells (the 5 m row became ocean).
findings.root_cause: The bootstrap MinDepth command is recorded in history with old_value equal to the dummy 0.0, and the undo reverts that command rather than restoring the replayed value.
findings.smallest_fix: Do not commit the initial MinDepth command when the domain's history already exists (add a flag to __init__ that from_version_control passes) and drop the undo(). Alternatively, save min_depth before the undo and restore it afterwards.

findings.title: Grid.from_center with angle_deg=±90 crashes: the grid is misdetected as cyclic ('cyclic_x is only supported for 360 degree domains')
findings.what: Grid.is_cyclic_x and SupergridBase.is_cyclic_x compare only the longitudes of the first and last supergrid columns. On a grid rotated 90°, those two columns have the same longitudes at different latitudes. from_supergrid_ds then passes cyclic_x=True to Grid(), which asserts lenx == 360 and fails. Building the grid any other way would still report is_cyclic_x=True to to_esmf_mesh, WW3 (SMPL closure) and get_bounding_boxes.
findings.trigger: Creating a regional grid aligned with a north-south coastline or estuary: Grid.from_center(lat, lon, w, h, res, angle_deg=90) or -90 (89° works).
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/mom6_forge/r10_rot90.py: from_center(30,-60,100e3,60e3,5e3,angle_deg=90) raises AssertionError: cyclic_x is only supported for 360 degree domains. Columns 0 and -1 both span lon -60.31..-59.69, but y is 30.45 vs 29.55. angle_deg=89 returns a grid with cyclic_x False.
findings.root_cause: The cyclic test checks longitude equality only (rtol=1e-5 on values around 300°) and ignores latitude.
findings.smallest_fix: Also require np.allclose(y[:,0], y[:,-1]), and compare the wrapped longitude difference ((x0-x1+180)%360-180) against an absolute tolerance, in both Grid.is_cyclic_x and SupergridBase.is_cyclic_x.

findings.title: Replaying a 'Clear manual mask' edit crashes: ClearMaskCommand.deserialize passes old_mask= that __init__ does not accept
findings.what: ClearMaskCommand.deserialize builds cls(topo, old_mask=old_mask), but __init__(self, topo, message=...) has no old_mask parameter. Any replay of a history that contains a mask clear raises TypeError: Topo.from_version_control, TopoCommandManager.checkout (branch switch) and redo after undoing a clear. The saved bathymetry can then no longer be loaded.
findings.trigger: Topo(..., git=True) or TopoEditor, then clear_user_mask() (the TopoEditor 'Clear user mask' button, set_from_dataset(mask_method='dataset'), or topo.user_mask = None), then Topo.from_version_control(domain_dir) or checkout/redo.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/mom6_forge/r5_vc.py [clr]: set user_mask, clear_user_mask(), Topo.from_version_control(t.domain_dir) raises TypeError: ClearMaskCommand.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'old_mask'.
findings.root_cause: The deserialize factory and the constructor signature diverged.
findings.smallest_fix: Add old_mask=None to ClearMaskCommand.__init__ (self.old_mask = old_mask if old_mask is not None else topo._user_mask), or construct cls(topo) in deserialize and set .old_mask afterwards.

findings.title: Suggested runoff smoothing radius is 0 or negative for rotated grids and grids finer than 200 m, so the runoff mapping crashes with 'rmax must be > 0 km'
findings.what: get_avg_resolution_km averages signed raw differences of center lon along i and of lat along j, assuming i points east and j north. For a grid rotated 90° that average is about 0; for 180° it is negative (-5 km for a 5 km grid). get_suggested_smoothing_params then truncates int(5*res) and returns rmax=0 (or -100) and fold=0 (or -200), and also returns 0 for any grid under 200 m. CrocoDash's RunoffConfigurator uses these defaults when rmax is not given, and gen_rof_maps fails in compute_smoothing_weights after writing the NN map. A 45° grid gets a value about 30% too small.
findings.trigger: A CrocoDash case with DROF/runoff and no rmax/fold, on a Grid.from_center grid with angle_deg near ±90 or 180, or any grid with cells under 200 m (estuary grids).
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/mom6_forge/r8_rmax.py: avg_res_km / suggested (rmax,fold): uniform 0.25° 25.7 / (100,200); from_center 5 km rot0 5.0 / (20,40); rot45 3.5 / (10,20); rot90 0.000 / (0,0); rot180 -5.0 / (-100,-200); 150 m rot0 0.15 / (0,0). compute_smoothing_weights raises ValueError('rmax must be > 0 km.') for any rmax <= 0.
findings.root_cause: The resolution estimate uses signed lat/lon deltas along index axes instead of the distance between neighbouring centers, and the rounding has no floor.
findings.smallest_fix: Compute neighbour spacing with haversine magnitudes between adjacent centers (both axes), and clamp the suggestion to rmax >= 1 km (fold >= rmax).

findings.title: iterative_fill counts land neighbours as zero-depth sources, so Cressman fallback cells at the coast come out too shallow
findings.what: In iterative_fill, filled_f = ~unfilled_2d marks every land cell as filled. Land depth in the Cressman output is 0, so each unfilled ocean cell is averaged with 0 m from every land neighbour. The docstring says land cells are never used, but they are. The cells this fallback fills are coastal by construction (mask says ocean, no source ocean point within L), so their depth is biased toward 0 and can drop to min_depth+0.1.
findings.trigger: Topo.set_from_dataset with depth_method='cressman', or the automatic Cressman choice (ratio >= 12x), when the mask (naturalearth, ocean_frac or user edits) marks as ocean a cell with no source ocean point within the Cressman radius. direct_cressman_interp then calls iterative_fill.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/mom6_forge/r7_misc.py: one unfilled ocean cell with two 100 m ocean neighbours and two land neighbours. Expected 100 m, observed 50.0 m.
findings.root_cause: The mask is applied to the cells to fill but not to the set of donor cells.
findings.smallest_fix: When mask is given, use filled_f = (~unfilled_2d & mask_2d).astype(float), so only filled ocean cells donate.

findings.title: Topo slicing (topo[j0:j1, i0:i1]) drops the user mask, so the sub-topo has a different land/sea mask
findings.what: Topo.__getitem__ copies only _depth into the new Topo. _user_mask (naturalearth, ocean_frac, TopoEditor edits, fill_inland_lakes_and_channels) and land_fillval are lost, so the sliced topo's tmask is recomputed from raw depth. Mask edits disappear from the topog, SCRIP, ESMF mesh, CICE kmt and WW3 mapsta written from it.
findings.trigger: Subsetting a finished bathymetry with topo[...] (for example to cut a smaller domain), then passing it to Case().
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/mom6_forge/r7_misc.py: set_flat(500), user_mask with two land cells, sub = t[0:3, 0:4]. Parent ocean count in that window is 10; the sliced topo has 12.
findings.root_cause: __getitem__ was written before the user-mask layer and copies raw depth only.
findings.smallest_fix: In __getitem__, also set new_topo._user_mask = self._user_mask[slices].copy() when it is not None, and copy land_fillval.

findings.title: Bathymetry with descending latitude gives an empty slice and a bare IndexError in diagnose_resolution
findings.what: SourceBathy._slice_to_domain uses .sel(lat=slice(lat_min-buf, lat_max+buf)), which returns nothing when the source latitude runs north to south (common for DEMs converted from GeoTIFF). set_from_dataset then fails in diagnose_resolution with 'IndexError: index 1 is out of bounds for axis 0 with size 0', which does not say what is wrong.
findings.trigger: Topo.set_from_dataset (or set_src / mpi_set_depth_from_xesmf) on a bathymetry file whose lat coordinate is descending.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/mom6_forge/r4c.py with r4_out/srcdesc.nc (global 0.25° analytic bathymetry, lat descending): IndexError at topo.py:1180 (dlat_deg = abs(src.lat[1]-src.lat[0])). The same data with ascending lat regrids exactly (r4_topo_lon.py).
findings.root_cause: The label slice assumes an ascending latitude coordinate.
findings.smallest_fix: Call self._ds = self._ds.sortby(self.lat_name) before slicing (or reverse the slice bounds when lat is decreasing), and raise a clear error if the slice is empty.

findings.title: Grid.from_supergrid rejects standard FRE hgrids (x units 'degree_east', y units 'degree_north') that check_supergrid accepts
findings.what: from_supergrid_ds asserts ds.x.units == ds.y.units and 'degree' in ds.x.units. FRE-NCtools make_hgrid and GFDL hgrids use 'degree_east' and 'degree_north', which check_supergrid explicitly allows. The load fails with 'Only degrees units are supported in supergrid files', which is wrong since the file is in degrees.
findings.trigger: Grid.from_supergrid('<FRE or GFDL ocean_hgrid.nc>'), Grid.subgrid_from_supergrid, or Topo.from_version_control on such a file.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/mom6_forge/r12_units.py: a mom6_forge hgrid with units changed to degree_east/degree_north passes check_supergrid, but from_supergrid raises AssertionError: Only degrees units are supported in supergrid files.
findings.root_cause: The assertion requires identical unit strings, which is stricter than the check_supergrid rule.
findings.smallest_fix: Assert 'degree' in ds.x.units and 'degree' in ds.y.units.

findings.title: generate_mask_from_landfrac_file reads ds.landfrac regardless of landfrac_name, and ignores xcoord_name/ycoord_name
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/mom6_forge/r14_misc.py: landfrac file with a variable named LANDFRAC; t.generate_mask_from_landfrac_file(path, 'LANDFRAC', 'lon', 'lat') raises AttributeError: 'Dataset' object has no attribute 'landfrac'.
findings.what: After checking that landfrac_name exists, the method regrids ds.landfrac. Any land-fraction file whose variable is not literally 'landfrac' (for example LANDFRAC from CAM/CLM) fails with AttributeError. xcoord_name and ycoord_name are validated but never used: xESMF looks up lat/lon itself, so files with other coordinate names also fail.
findings.trigger: Topo.generate_mask_from_landfrac_file(path, 'LANDFRAC', 'lon', 'lat') or any landfrac_name other than 'landfrac'.
findings.root_cause: The variable name is hardcoded.
findings.smallest_fix: Use regridder(ds[landfrac_name]) and rename xcoord_name/ycoord_name to lon/lat before building the Regridder.

findings.title: Grid file metadata gives wrong units: CICE grid tlat/tlon are radians labelled degrees, hgrid angle_dx is degrees labelled radians
findings.what: write_cice_grid stores np.deg2rad(tlat/tlon) with units 'degrees_north'/'degrees_east'. to_ds writes angle_dx (computed in degrees by mom6_angle_calculation_method) with units 'radians'. Neither model reads these attributes (CICE popgrid_nc reads ulat/ulon/angle/anglet/htn/hte; MOM6 recomputes angles; rm6 applies np.radians to angle_dx), but any tool or user that trusts the attrs gets values off by a factor of 57.3.
findings.trigger: Any case with CICE (cice_grid_*.nc) or any written ocean_hgrid, read by a units-aware tool (cf-xarray, pint, plotting).
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/mom6_forge/r3_writers.py: cice tlat units 'degrees_north', values 0.532..0.620 (radians); hgrid angle_dx attrs {'units': 'radians'} while from_center grids hold values like -29.9 (degrees, r2_angles.py).
findings.root_cause: The unit attributes were copied without matching the values written.
findings.smallest_fix: Set tlat/tlon units to 'radians' in write_cice_grid, and angle_dx units to 'degrees' in SupergridBase.to_ds.

also_noticed: mapping.py:122 extract_coastline_mask pads with mode='wrap' in both axes, so on regional grids the open-boundary row or column opposite a land edge is flagged as coastline (r13 at angle 30: 12 east-column cells). Low impact today because only ocean source cells (zero runoff) reach those cells.
utils.py longitude_slicer (around lines 118-129) drops the east end: longitude_slicer(ds,[10,20]) on 1° data returns 10..19. Every current caller pads by 0.5-1.5°, so it is masked.

The known longitude_slicer seam-midpoint ValueError (QUEUE) is also reached from Topo.set_from_dataset: a 0..360 bathymetry with a grid centred on 0° (-5..5) raises 'The longitude of the data doesn't seem to include the longitude of the grid' (r4_topo_lon.py x-5_src360). GEBCO with a domain centred on 180° is the mirror case.
topo.py qmask forces the four corner q-points to land even on cyclic grids.
grid.py ~828-848: dxCu/dyCv use np.roll, so the last column/row wraps on non-cyclic grids; angle_q is labelled dims (ny,nx) but has shape (nyp,nxp). Nothing downstream reads them.
Topo.max_depth uses raw depth including cells masked to land, so the MAXIMUM_DEPTH CrocoDash puts in MOM_input (case.py:785) can exceed the deepest written depth (harmless).
utils.py get_avg_resolution_km calls xr.open_dataset(mesh) unconditionally, so passing an xr.Dataset fails.
grid.py:632-636 Grid.from_supergrid ignores the name argument for files whose names do not end in .nc (operator precedence); write_supergrid(path=None) raises TypeError on os.path.basename(None).
CrocoDash/forcing/runoff.py:21,58 documents rmax as meters, but mom6_forge takes km (a user passing 50000 gets a 50000 km radius).
_supergrid.py from_center docstring says angle_deg=45 points the x-axis NE. The code (correctly) makes the y-axis point NE and the x-axis SE, angle_dx=-45.
vgrid.py VGrid.hyperbolic docstring calls ratio 'top to bottom'; the code uses dzbot = ratio*dz0 (bottom/top).
Topo.from_version_control adds two commits (MinDepth + UNDO) to the library history on every load.
set_spoon/set_bowl use the first T-point as the domain origin instead of the west/south edge (half-cell offset from MOM6's TOPO_CONFIG).
CrocoDash case.py:421 writes ww3_grid.inp with the default cpl_dt=1800, while _set_ww3_timesteps puts the real WAV interval in user_nl_ww3 (which overrides it).

mapping.py _cached_cell_areas is a process-global cache keyed by file path, so a mesh rewritten at the same path in the same process gets stale areas (unlikely in CrocoDash because session ids differ).
topo.py diagnose_resolution measures source dx at the slice's southernmost latitude; its docstring says 1e6 source points while the code uses 2e6.
Topo.from_topo_file defaults min_depth=0.0 instead of reading the file's min_depth attribute.
fill_inland_lakes_and_channels uses xarray .shift (no wrap), so channels across a cyclic seam are not filled.
checked_ok: write_supergrid -> Grid.from_supergrid round trip: tlon bit-identical, tarea equal (r3_writers.py)
ESMF mesh write -> Grid.from_esmf_mesh round trip for an unrotated grid: tlon/qlat match (r3_writers.py)
Mask consistency: topog mask, SCRIP grid_imask, ESMF elementMask and CICE kmt all 45 ocean cells; a 5 m cell under min_depth=10 is land everywhere (r3_writers.py)
CICE htn/hte match independent spherical edge lengths exactly (cm); ulat/ulon/angle/anglet in radians; CICE reads only ulat/ulon/angle/anglet/htn/hte (checked against ice_grid.F90 popgrid_nc)
SCRIP grid_area vs supergrid quadrant areas: 4e-6 relative; mesh elementArea equals the supergrid block sum exactly (r3_writers.py); Grid.tarea is off by 1.6e-3 (known #126)
VGrid uniform/hyperbolic: sum(dz)==depth, all positive, write/from_file round trip, from cell_center and cell_interface reconstruct dz exactly (r3_writers.py)

angle_dx sign and magnitude on from_center grids (0, 30, -45°) within 0.25° of an independent bearing calculation; polar EPSG:3995 grid agrees except within about 1° of the pole (r2_angles.py, r2b.py)
Topo.set_from_dataset (xesmf, mask_method='dataset') against an analytic bathymetry: exact for source -180..180 or 0..360 with grids at 355..365, 170..180, -60..-50 (r4_topo_lon.py)
generate_mask_from_naturalearth gives identical masks for xstart -10/350/710 (r6_ne.py, cached Natural Earth data, no download)

Runoff NN and smoothed maps conserve runoff (the _check_runoff_conserved check passes in r1/r13); compute_smoothing_weights adjacency correct for unrotated grids (reading)
get_bounding_boxes anchoring for a 350..370 grid gives -10..10 with crosses False (reading)

not_covered: ESMF mesh pole-row collapse/expansion and tripolar/cyclic global meshes (reconstruct_from_esmf_mesh on tx2_3-like meshes)

mpi_set_depth_from_xesmf and the mapping.py main() CLI / esmpy map path (generate_ESMF_map_via_esmpy)
Antimeridian-crossing sources for Cressman (KD-tree on xyz should be fine; not run)
Channel width files as applied by MOM6 (only read the writer/loader)
An end-to-end CrocoDash Case() run through mom6_forge writers; the writers were exercised directly instead, to keep load low

findings.title: CESM-POP (and native MOM6) velocities are grid-relative but are regridded as eastward/northward, so the IC and OBC currents are rotated by the source grid's ANGLE
findings.what: POP's UVEL/VVEL are 'Velocity in grid-x/grid-y direction'. CESM_POP_OUTPUT hands them to regional-mom6 unchanged, and regional-mom6 treats u_var_name/v_var_name as earth-relative: it rotates only by the target grid's angle. The POP grid's ANGLE is never applied, even though the files carry it and it ends up in the raw file. The boundary and initial currents therefore point the wrong way wherever the POP grid is not aligned with lat/lon. CESM_MOM_OUTPUT has the same problem: MOM6 'uo'/'vo' are grid-x/y on tripolar or rotated parents.
findings.trigger: configure_forcings(product_name='CESM_POP_OUTPUT', function_name='get_cesm_single_variable_data'), using CESM-HR FOSI (the default path) or LENS2 (dataset_path=/gdex/.../CESM2-LE/...), for a domain in the mid/high-latitude Northern Hemisphere, then process_forcings. Real ANGLE values at the U point: FOSI-HR tx0.1v3 is -19 deg in the Gulf of Alaska, +13 deg in the Labrador Sea, -15 deg in the Nordic Seas, -8 deg in the North Sea and +6 deg in the Gulf of Maine (up to +/-90 deg north of 60N). LENS2 gx1v7 is +31 deg in the Nordic Seas, +12 deg in the North Sea and -11 deg in the Gulf of Alaska. The tropics and the Southern Hemisphere are ~0.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/raw_data/r3_pop_rotation.py (synthetic POP tseries from mkpop.py with ANGLE=30 deg, UVEL=100 cm/s, VVEL=0, run through utils.fetch_raw_chunk(get_cesm_single_variable_data) then forcing.mom6._regrid_obc_chunk onto a plain lat-lon segment). Expected u=0.866, v=0.5 m/s. Observed: 'MOM6 OBC u (m/s): mean 1.0  v (m/s): mean 0.0'. The raw file carries ANGLE=30 deg, unused. The ANGLE values above came from reading ANGLE/ULAT/ULONG in one FOSI and one LENS2 UVEL file.
findings.root_cause: The product metadata contract (u_var_name/v_var_name) assumes earth-relative components, and neither the CESM readers nor regional-mom6 rotate source-grid vectors. Separately, u/v are also mapped to TLAT/TLONG although UVEL/VVEL sit at ULAT/ULONG.
findings.smallest_fix: In read_single_variable_tseries_data, when UVEL and VVEL are both read for CESM_POP_OUTPUT, replace them with earth-relative components using the file's ANGLE (radians, U grid): u_e = UVEL*cos(ANGLE) - VVEL*sin(ANGLE), v_n = UVEL*sin(ANGLE) + VVEL*cos(ANGLE). Do the same for CESM_MOM_OUTPUT when the source carries an angle (sin_rot/cos_rot or geolon/geolat). Also point u/v lat/lon metadata at ULAT/ULONG.

findings.title: CESM_MOM_OUTPUT hard-codes the NOLEAP calendar: nesting inside a GREGORIAN parent sets the child to NO_LEAP and crashes the OBC regrid on Feb 29
findings.what: CESM_MOM_OUTPUT.calendar is fixed to NOLEAP. configure_forcings therefore xmlchanges CALENDAR=NO_LEAP on the child, and the OBC regrid encodes the parent's times with calendar 'noleap', whatever calendar the parent run used. A parent made by CrocoDash with GLORYS runs GREGORIAN, so any window that contains Feb 29 of a leap year fails. Outside such windows the child silently runs a different calendar from its parent.
findings.trigger: Nest a child domain with product_name='CESM_MOM_OUTPUT', function_name='get_mom6_output_data', dataset_path=<history dir of a GLORYS-forced (GREGORIAN) parent run>, and a date_range that spans 2020-02-29. Then run process_forcings (bc).
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/raw_data/r7_mom_calendar.py: synthetic native-MOM6 daily output (gregorian, 2020-02-27..03-02) goes through fetch_raw_chunk(get_mom6_output_data) and then _regrid_obc_chunk. Observed: 'product calendar: Calendar(cf=noleap, cesm=NO_LEAP, mom6=noleap)' and then 'OBC regrid failed: ValueError invalid day number provided in cftime.DatetimeNoLeap(2020, 2, 29, 12, ...)'. Expected: the parent's own calendar is kept (GREGORIAN), or a clear refusal at configure time.
findings.root_cause: The calendar is product-level class metadata. For CESM_MOM_OUTPUT it really depends on the parent run that the user points at, and it is never read from the files' time:calendar.
findings.smallest_fix: Read time:calendar from the first file under dataset_path at configure time (or take a 'calendar' function_override) and use it for both the CALENDAR xmlchange and the OBC/IC encoding. At minimum, refuse at configure time when the parent's calendar is not noleap.

findings.title: A raw chunk left half-written by a killed process is reused on resume: fetch_raw_chunk only checks the 4 magic bytes
findings.what: Every access method writes straight to its final file name (ds.to_netcdf(path)). The resume check in fetch_raw_chunk accepts any file whose first 4 bytes are an HDF5/CDF signature, and a netCDF4 file killed mid-write has those bytes. A resumed process_forcings skips the fetch and regrids a file that is missing variables, or whose last variable is entirely fill (NaN). CESM's per-variable subset cache (subset_dataset) is skipped on existence alone. The partial-file check that exists was meant for exactly this case, but it never fires.
findings.trigger: process_forcings is killed (PBS walltime, OOM kill, Ctrl-C, or the known silent exit) while a GET worker is writing <boundary>_unprocessed.<dates>.nc or ic_unprocessed.nc, and process_forcings is then rerun to resume, as the docs recommend.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/raw_data/r4_writer.py, killed with SIGKILL partway through writing a reference_ocean raw chunk, then r4_resume.py. Kill at 117 MB: is_valid_netcdf True, 'fetch_raw_chunk returned without refetching', and the file holds only 'u' (100% NaN) with temp/salt/ssh/v missing, so the REGRID-side open fails later with "'Dataset' object has no attribute 'temp'". Kill at 822 MB: all 5 variables are present, salt is 100% NaN in 30/30 records, and the file is still accepted. Expected: the partial file is detected and fetched again.
findings.root_cause: Non-atomic writes in the access methods (and in subset_dataset's cache), combined with a validity check that only reads the file signature. The same pattern applies to obc._merge_boundary's merged file and to the IC files checked by _all_written.
findings.smallest_fix: In fetch_raw_chunk, call the access method with a temporary output_filename (e.g. '.<name>.part') and os.replace it onto the final name only after the method returns. Do the same with tmp+replace in subset_dataset. Any '.part' file left over is then never mistaken for a finished chunk.

findings.title: CESM tseries readers swallow 'no files found' and missing variables; the failure surfaces later as an unrelated FileNotFoundError or KeyError
findings.what: get_cesm_single_variable_data / get_mom6_single_variable_data only print 'No files found for variable: X'. When nothing matches they print 'No subset files to merge ...; skipping merge' and return normally, without writing output_filename. When some variables match, they merge whatever was found. get_mom6_output_data only logs a warning for missing variables. In every case the access method 'succeeds'.
findings.trigger: A CESM-POP/LENS2/MOM6 case whose date_range is outside the archive, whose dataset_path or member is wrong, or whose archive lacks one variable (e.g. SSH in another directory). The YYYYMM end-of-file parsing known from #347 also produces 0 matches for windows late in a month. The user then sees either rm6's 'Initial condition file not found at .../ic_unprocessed.nc. Please ensure that the files are named in the format ic_unprocessed.nc' (IC), 'No files for [south] — preceding phase produced no output.' (OBC), or a KeyError for 'SSH' deep in Segment.regrid_velocity_tracers. None of these names the real cause.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/raw_data/r2_pop_missing.py (synthetic POP archive for 2000). (a) dates 2005-01-01..02: prints '0 file(s) found' for each variable, and then 'fetch_raw_chunk returned r2/raw_a/ic_unprocessed.nc exists: False' with no exception. (b) SSH files removed: no exception, and the raw file's data vars are ['ANGLE','SALT','TEMP','UVEL','VVEL']. Expected: a ValueError or FileNotFoundError naming the missing variables, dataset_path and date window.
findings.root_cause: read_single_variable_tseries_data and subset_dataset treat an empty file list per variable as non-fatal. The merge step skips silently, and fetch_raw_chunk ignores the method's return value and never checks that output_filename was written.
findings.smallest_fix: In read_single_variable_tseries_data, raise FileNotFoundError when any requested variable has no files after parse_dataset and the member filter, and list the variables, dataset_path and dates. Make get_mom6_output_data raise instead of warn. Optionally, have fetch_raw_chunk assert that the output file exists after the call. Related: #335 (1.1) adds a coverage check at configure time for dates, but not for missing variables.

findings.title: GLOFAS get_global_data_with_python saves a zip archive under a .nc name and requests every year x month x day combination
findings.what: The request sets download_format='zip', but the result is written to output_folder/'glofas_data.nc' and that path is returned. The file is a zip archive, so xr.open_dataset on it fails. The dates are also sent as independent hyear/hmonth/hday sets, which CDS expands as a Cartesian product. A window that crosses a month or year boundary therefore returns many days outside the window.
findings.trigger: A user fetches raw GLOFAS discharge by hand (off the forcing path, which uses a processed file) with GLOFAS.get_global_data_with_python(dates=['2019-12-30','2020-01-02'], ...).
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/raw_data/r5_misc.py, section (h), with cdsapi.Client mocked. Observed request: hyear ['2019','2020'], hmonth ['01','12'], hday ['01','02','30','31'], download_format 'zip', target r5/glofas_data.nc. That is 16 days (including Jan 2019 and Dec 2020) for a 4-day window. That a zip archive comes back was judged from reading only: the ecmwf-datastores client docs use download_format='unarchived' to get the raw file.
findings.root_cause: The request was copied from the CDS web form, which offers a zip download, and the hyear/hmonth/hday keys are built as sets instead of being matched to the requested days.
findings.smallest_fix: Use download_format='unarchived' (or unzip into output_folder and return the extracted .nc). After download, cut the result to [start, end] (or issue one request per month).

findings.title: get_glorys_data writes the output folder unquoted into the copernicusmarine command, so the generated script breaks for paths with spaces
findings.what: The CLI-script access method (GLORYS.get_glorys_data_script_for_cli, CrocoDash's default function_name) calls rm6.get_glorys_data. That function writes '-o {path} -f {segment_name}.nc' without quotes. If the inputdir contains a space, bash splits the path, and copernicusmarine gets a truncated -o value plus a stray positional argument.
findings.trigger: A CrocoDash case whose inputdir contains a space (common on laptops, e.g. '~/My Cases/...'), configured with the default get_glorys_data_script_for_cli, followed by running the generated get_glorys_data script.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/raw_data/r5_misc.py, section (a). The script line ends '-o r5/with space -f north_unprocessed....nc', and shell word-splitting gives -o='r5/with', then 'space', then '-f'. Expected: -o "r5/with space".
findings.root_cause: The f-string builds the shell command without quoting (no shlex.quote). Not fixed on regional-mom6 origin/main (same line 213).
findings.smallest_fix: Quote the arguments: -o {shlex.quote(str(path))} -f {shlex.quote(segment_name + '.nc')}.

findings.title: configure_forcings gives vague errors for an unknown product ('Product / Data Path is not supported quite yet') or access method (bare KeyError)
findings.what: Both a misspelled product and a real product that is not a ForcingProduct (e.g. 'gebco') raise 'Product / Data Path is not supported quite yet', with no list of valid products. ConditionsConfigurator.validate_args has a helpful message with that list, but it is never reached. A misspelled or wrong-product function_name raises a bare KeyError('get_glorys_data_from_rdaa') from get_function_default_args, with no list of the product's access methods.
findings.trigger: case.configure_forcings(..., product_name='GLORYS', function_name='get_glorys_data_from_rdaa'), or product_name='glorys12'.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/raw_data/r5_misc.py, section (b). ProductRegistry.get_function_default_args('glorys','get_glorys_data_from_rdaa') raises KeyError('get_glorys_data_from_rdaa'). The product message comes from reading case.py:589-593.
findings.root_cause: configure_forcings checks the product before the configurator's better validation, and never checks function_name against ProductRegistry.list_access_methods.
findings.smallest_fix: In configure_forcings, raise ValueError(f"Unknown forcing product {product_name!r}; known: {sorted(ProductRegistry.products)}"). Also check function_name in ProductRegistry.list_access_methods(product_name) and raise a ValueError that lists them.

also_noticed: reference_waves spectrum integrates to Hs ~3.1 m, while the comment says 'a 2m/8s swell (Hs=2, Tp=8)'. The hs variable is unused and alpha is fixed (CrocoDash/raw_data_access/datasets/reference.py:446). Cosmetic, but misleading for anyone checking WW3 boundary amplitudes.

reference_ocean / reference_ice produce latitudes beyond +/-90 (up to 91.0) and overlapping longitudes (-181..181, 725 columns) for polar or encircling boxes (reference.py:129-130, 331-332). xESMF warns 'Latitude is outside of [-90, 90]', but a test regrid stayed exact. Cosmetic.

GLORYS RDA raw files keep the first day's time valid_min=valid_max (613620), so every later record is outside the declared valid range. netCDF4-python, NCO and ncview-style readers would mask them. xarray ignores it (glorys.py:94-106).

mom6_forge longitude_slicer returns up to ~1.6 GLORYS cells short of the requested east edge. Asking for -1.3..1.3 gave -1.25..1.167. This is harmless with buf=1, but a function_override of buf near 0 would leave the domain edge uncovered (mom6_forge/utils.py:119-126).
CESM_POP_OUTPUT maps UVEL/VVEL to TLAT/TLONG although they sit at ULAT/ULONG, a half-cell placement offset (~0.5 deg on gx1v7) (cesm_ocean_output.py:45-48). Fix together with the rotation finding.

ERA5 build_era5_spectra_request: a non-crossing box that ends exactly at 180 (170..180) raises 'crossing 180E', and an encircling box (-180..180) becomes the area -181..-179, a 2-degree sliver (era5.py:140-142). #348 (1.1) territory.

ERA5 decode rebuilds longitudes with linspace(first, last). If MARS returns unsigned (GRIB2-style) longitudes for a box across 0 deg (354..6), the axis would come out wrong. Unverified, needs a real pull (era5.py:196-199).
datasets/utils.write_bash_curl_script: 'mkdir -p {output_folder}' is unquoted, so it breaks on paths with spaces (utils.py:47). This is separate from #349's open-before-mkdir.
get_mom6_output_data: a request that includes Feb 29 against its NOLEAP product calendar fails with a cftime ValueError from date2num rather than a clear message (cesm_ocean_output.py:245).
GLORYS has no data south of 80S. Antarctic boxes below -80 are clipped silently by the latitude slice (glorys.py:101), with no warning.

parse_dataset falls back to os.walk over the whole dataset_path for any variable without its own subdirectory (e.g. LENS2 MARBL variables), which is very slow on GDEX (cesm_ocean_output.py:534). Performance only.
ProductRegistry.load assigns a local 'loaded' (no-op) (registry.py:87). cice.py:524 and ic.py:87 never close the datasets they open. Minor leaks.
CESM_MOM_OUTPUT velocities have the same grid-relative problem as POP on tripolar/rotated parents (covered in finding 1, no separate repro).
checked_ok: GLORYS RDA reader on real local files (two days, tiny boxes): a 0..360 box (280..280.5) and a Greenwich box (-0.3..0.3) both give monotonic longitude labels in the request's convention, buf padding on lat, and hours-since-1950 times. RDA holds exactly one file per date for 1993-2026, and a missing date raises a clear FileNotFoundError. Repro: r1_rda.py.

copernicusmarine 2.0.1 transposes min/max longitude into [-180, 360), so 0..360 OBC boxes and antimeridian IC boxes (lon_max > 180) from get_bounding_boxes are accepted by get_glorys_data_from_cds_api. Checked by reading the installed package.
POP cm-based units: z_t/z_t_150m (centimeters), UVEL/VVEL (centimeter/s) and SSH (centimeter) are all converted to m by regional-mom6's pint path. Repro log r3.log shows 'Converted ...' for each.

reference_ocean: depth is layer centres (positive down), temp/salt/u/v/ssh have the expected dims and daily records include the end day, and the variables filter works. A polar-box output regrids exactly with xESMF despite lat > 90. Repro: r5_misc.py (e), r6_polar_ref.py.

Idempotency across configurations: ConditionsConfigurator.stale_outputs removes extract_forcings/raw_data and regridded_data when dates, product, function_args or chunking change. So the undated ic_unprocessed.nc and the CESM per-variable subset caches are not reused for a changed configuration. WW3 staging has an equivalent check. Checked by reading mom6.py:723-760 and ww3.py:590-607.
bbox_mask handles both 0..360 and -180..180 sources and antimeridian arcs (offset modulo 360). Checked by reading.
CESM-WW3-JRA: whole-day inclusive 6-hourly stamps, the Feb 29 -> Feb 28 mapping, cyclic seam windows (_axis_indices/_window_runs), and refusal of out-of-range requests. Checked by reading.
make_dates_end_inclusive is used by the CDS API and CLI-script paths. The RDA, reference and ERA5 paths are whole-day inclusive by construction. Checked by reading.

ProductRegistry: case-insensitive lookup, required_args enforcement in __init_subclass__, and get_function_default_args excluding required args and **kwargs. write_metadata drops marbl_var_names unless include_marbl_tracers is set. Checked by reading.
_ERA5 cdsapi client env juggling restores CDSAPI_RC, and GET workers are processes, so the env change is not shared. Checked by reading.
not_covered: Real downloads: GLORYS via the Copernicus API or CLI script, ERA5 2D spectra GRIB decode, and GLOFAS cdsapi (no network allowed), so the ERA5 longitude-axis convention and the GLOFAS zip payload are unverified against live services.
CICE_RESTART subsetting on real tripole grid files (#347 territory), and the CICE regrid of reference_ice for polar boxes.
CESM_MOM_OUTPUT.get_mom6_single_variable_data and the LENS2 member filter on real archives (one LENS2 and one FOSI header read only).
Full end-to-end process_forcings with CESM_POP_OUTPUT on real FOSI/LENS2 data (TRIAGE item 1 territory). The rotation finding was shown with synthetic POP files plus real ANGLE values.
GEBCO/SRTM/SeaWiFS script and python methods beyond reading (#349 covers their defaults).

verify:mom6_forge-a1.verdict_reason: The code does what the finding says, and nothing upstream guards against it. RunoffConfigurator is required for every DROF compset, and its process() (CrocoDash/forcing/runoff.py:180) calls mapping.gen_rof_maps. That calls generate_ESMF_map_via_xesmf with map_overlap left at its default of True and method nearest_d2s, and normalize_deg is applied to the destination and source latitudes and longitudes. My own repro calls gen_rof_maps exactly as CrocoDash does. It gets band-wide (or column-wide) source capture for a domain that crosses 0°, a domain with an edge exactly at 0°, and a domain that crosses the equator. Patching only the overlap test gives the correct cell counts. No open issue or PR tracks this. TRIAGE.md, QUEUE.md and the baseline have nothing on it. CrocoDash #187 is about runoff mapping speed, not this. The fix existed only in mom6_forge PR #128, which was closed without merging.
verify:mom6_forge-a1.title: Runoff map: the map_overlap mask in generate_ESMF_map_via_xesmf fails for domains that cross 0° longitude, have an edge at 0°, or cross the equator, so the domain receives runoff from the whole latitude band or longitude column
verify:mom6_forge-a1.location: CrocoDash/visualCaseGen/external/mom6_forge/mom6_forge/mapping.py:643-659 (643-644 normalize destination lon and lat, 645-646 min/max, 649-650 normalize source lon and lat, 652-659 mask). Reached via CrocoDash/forcing/runoff.py:180 → mapping.py:1161 (gen_rof_maps → generate_ESMF_map_via_xesmf, map_overlap=True by default)
verify:mom6_forge-a1.what:
With map_overlap=True, which gen_rof_maps always uses, generate_ESMF_map_via_xesmf builds a box from the destination mesh. It takes normalize_deg() (mod 360) of every node longitude and latitude and then the plain min and max. Any source runoff cell outside that box is masked out.

There are three failure cases:
1. **Domain crosses 0°**, e.g. -5..5E. The node longitudes become 355..360 and 0..5, so the box is 0..~360 and no longitude is masked.
2. **Domain has an edge exactly at 0°**, e.g. -10..0E, or 350..360 in 0-360 convention. The node at 0 or 360 becomes 0 and is the minimum, so the box is again 0..~360.
3. **Domain crosses the equator**, e.g. -5..5N. The latitudes become 0..5 and 355..360, so the latitude box is 0..~360 and no latitude is masked. Source latitudes go through the same mod.

Because the method is nearest_d2s, every unmasked source cell sends its runoff to its nearest coastline cell in the domain. The regional ocean therefore receives the river runoff of the whole latitude band (cases 1 and 2) or the whole longitude column (case 3). _check_runoff_conserved still passes, because the extra runoff is conserved, only placed in the wrong ocean.
verify:mom6_forge-a1.repro_command:
cd /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/verify/mom6_forge-a1 && source ../../env.sh && timeout 900 $PY -u v1_overlap.py

Script: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/verify/mom6_forge-a1/v1_overlap.py
- Source: a near-global 3° all-ocean rof mesh, from Grid(lenx=357, leny=150, resolution=3, xstart=-180, ystart=-75), Topo.set_flat and write_esmf_mesh.
- Destination: 10x10° domains at 2°, with the west 2 columns set to land.
- Each domain: mapping.gen_rof_maps(rof_mesh_path=rof_mesh, ocn_mesh_path=ocn, output_dir=out, mapping_file_prefix=..., rmax=None, fold=None). The script then lists the source cells that have S>0 in the nn map.

Fix check: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/verify/mom6_forge-a1/v2_fixcheck.py runs the same script with the overlap block patched to compare latitude raw and use a circular longitude window.
verify:mom6_forge-a1.expected:
Only source cells inside the domain's lon/lat box get a weight: about 12 to 16 cells per 10x10° domain with 3° source cells. This is what the patched run gives:
- [pm] -5..5E: 16 cells, lon -4.5..4.5
- [edge0] -10..0E: 12 cells, lon -7.5..-1.5
- [eq] -5..5N: 12 cells, lat -4.5..4.5
verify:mom6_forge-a1.observed:
Unpatched audited code:
- RESULT [east] domain lon 5..15 lat 40..50: 12 src cells mapped; their lon 7.5..13.5, lat 40.5..49.5 (correct)
- RESULT [pm] domain lon -5..5 lat 40..50: 476 src cells mapped; their lon -178.5..175.5, lat 40.5..49.5 (all 119 longitudes in the band)
- RESULT [edge0] domain lon -10..0 lat 40..50: 472 src cells mapped; their lon -178.5..175.5, lat 40.5..49.5
- RESULT [eq] domain lon 5..15 lat -5..5: 150 src cells mapped; their lon 7.5..13.5, lat -73.5..73.5 (all 50 latitudes)
- RESULT [south] domain lon 5..15 lat -50..-40: 12 src cells mapped (correct; a domain entirely in the southern hemisphere is fine)

gen_rof_maps' conservation check passes in every case.
verify:mom6_forge-a1.root_cause:
The bounding-box test treats both coordinates as linear [0,360) ranges:
1. normalize_deg (np.mod(x+360, 360)) is applied to latitude (lines 644 and 650), so a latitude range that crosses 0 splits into 0..a and 360-b..360.
2. min/max over normalized longitudes (line 645) cannot describe an arc that contains the 0/360 cut. A node at exactly 0° or 360° maps to 0 and becomes the minimum, which also produces a near-global box.
verify:mom6_forge-a1.smallest_fix:
In generate_ESMF_map_via_xesmf, change the overlap test:
- **Latitude:** compare raw latitudes; drop normalize_deg on lines 644 and 650.
- **Longitude:** use a circular window. Take the sorted unique normalized node longitudes. The window starts after the largest circular gap and its width is 360 minus that gap. A source cell is inside when mod(src_lon - start, 360) <= width.
- Mask the source wherever the cell is not inside in both longitude and latitude.

This is what closed, unmerged mom6_forge PR #128 (_lon_window, commit 1812c4d on branch fix-map-overlap-seam-latitude-masking) implements. It can be re-landed with its tests. A patched copy of this logic gives the expected counts for all five domains in v2_fixcheck.py.
verify:mom6_forge-a1.fixed_on_main: No. mom6_forge origin/main (83d7692) still has the same code at mapping.py:643-650, and neither of the 2 commits after the pin (#126 tarea fix, #155 file I/O) touches it. The only fix was PR #128, which was closed without merging on 2026-09-13; it was stacked on #127, which was merged.
verify:mom6_forge-a1.related: mom6_forge PR #128 (closed, unmerged; the fix). mom6_forge PR #125 (closed; its description first raised the latitude half). mom6_forge PR #127 (merged; the base #128 was stacked on). CrocoDash issue #187 (runoff mapping speed; not the same bug). Not in TRIAGE.md or QUEUE.md.

findings.title: Case() does not normalise caseroot/inputdir: relative paths end up in user_nl_mom and the mesh xml, a relative caseroot is re-rooted under $HOME, and '~' is refused
findings.what: Case stores caseroot and inputdir as given (Path(x)) and passes them unchanged to visualCaseGen as CASEROOT and CUSTOM_GRID_PATH. (1) A relative inputdir is written verbatim as INPUTDIR in user_nl_mom and as OCN/ICE/WAV_DOMAIN_MESH and MASK_MESH, so MOM6 and CMEPS resolve them against RUNDIR at run time and cannot find the files. (2) For a relative caseroot, visualCaseGen's create_case runs create_newcase at $HOME/<relative path>, while CrocoDash and the xmlchange helper use the cwd-relative path. The result is a misleading 'Cannot write to $HOME/...' or, if that parent exists, a case created in $HOME, then '[Errno 2] No such file' from the first xmlchange, and the $HOME case is left orphaned. (3) A caseroot or inputdir starting with '~' is refused with 'Path ~/... doesn't exist' even though the directory exists.
findings.trigger: Python API or a YAML create config (recipe.create_case_from_yaml passes config['case'] straight to Case) with caseroot/inputdir like 'cases/x', './input/x' or '~/croc_cases/x'.
findings.repro: Scripts in /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/vcg/. t_relinput.py: os.chdir(S); Case(..., inputdir=Path('input/audit_vcg_relin')). Expected absolute paths; observed user_nl_mom 'INPUTDIR = input/audit_vcg_relin/ocn' and env_run.xml OCN_DOMAIN_MESH=ICE_DOMAIN_MESH=WAV_DOMAIN_MESH=MASK_MESH='input/audit_vcg_relin/ocn/ESMF_mesh_vcgg_ab79ed.nc'. t_relcase.py: caseroot=Path('cases/audit_vcg_relcase') gives 'RuntimeError: Cannot write to /glade/u/home/manishrv/cases/audit_vcg_relcase'. t_relcase2.py with HOME=<scratch>/fakehome containing cases/: create_newcase --case <fakehome>/cases/audit_vcg_relcase2 succeeds, then 'Error running ./xmlchange OCN_GRID=vcgg --non-local in cases/audit_vcg_relcase2: [Errno 2]'; afterwards the HOME case still exists and the cwd case does not. t_tilde.py: inputdir='~/scratch/.../input/audit_vcg_tilde' (parent exists after expanduser) gives 'Case configuration failed: Path ~/scratch/.../input doesn't exist'; same for caseroot.
findings.root_cause: case.py:170-171 keep the raw paths, with no expanduser() or resolve(). They reach cvars CUSTOM_GRID_PATH (case.py:903) and CASEROOT (case.py:1060), which visualCaseGen uses verbatim for the mesh xmlchanges and INPUTDIR. case_creator.py:124-125 anchors a non-absolute CASEROOT at Path.home(), while xmlchange (case_tools.py:144,160) and CrocoDash use it relative to cwd. _write_state also records the unresolved paths.
findings.smallest_fix: In Case.__init__, before init_args_check, set caseroot = Path(caseroot).expanduser().resolve() and inputdir = Path(inputdir).expanduser().resolve(), and use those everywhere (state included). Optionally, make case_creator.py resolve against cwd instead of Path.home().

findings.title: override=True rmtree's <CIME_OUTPUT_ROOT>/<case name> whatever it is: a case named 'archive', 'tmp' or 'croc_input' wipes that shared scratch directory
findings.what: With override=True, Case() calls shutil.rmtree on Path(cime.cime_output_root)/caseroot.name without checking that this directory is the old case's build/run dir. On Derecho and Casper, CIME_OUTPUT_ROOT is /glade/derecho/scratch/$USER. That directory also holds archive/ (DOUT_S_ROOT=$CIME_OUTPUT_ROOT/archive/$CASE for every case), tmp/, and the croc_input/ tree CLAUDE.md recommends for inputdirs. A case whose basename matches any of these deletes the whole shared directory.
findings.trigger: Case(caseroot='~/croc_cases/archive' (or 'tmp', 'croc_input', ...), override=True, ...): for example, re-running a throwaway test case called 'tmp'.
findings.repro: Reading only; a safe dry-run (rmtree stubbed, creation aborted) was blocked by the session's permission classifier, so nothing was executed. Evidence: case.py:205-212 builds case_dirs=[inputdir, caseroot, Path(self.cime.cime_output_root)/self.caseroot.name] and calls _remove_previous (shutil.rmtree) on each when override. cime.cime_output_root printed as /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv (t_two_roots.py output). `ls -d /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/{archive,tmp,croc_input}` shows all three exist, and archive/ holds other cases' archives (bgc_fe_test_derecho, cool_obc, ...). Expected: only the old case's EXEROOT/RUNDIR are removed. Observed by reading: the whole <root>/<name> tree is removed.
findings.root_cause: The override cleanup assumes <CIME_OUTPUT_ROOT>/<CASE> belongs to that case. What create_newcase --handle-preexisting-dirs actually checks is only EXEROOT and RUNDIR (<root>/<CASE>/bld and /run).
findings.smallest_fix: Remove only <root>/<name>/bld and <root>/<name>/run (or EXEROOT/RUNDIR read from the old caseroot's env xml when it exists), and refuse with a clear error if <root>/<name> contains anything else.

findings.title: Case() accepts MOM6 compsets without %REGIONAL (its own docstring suggests them), so a regional grid gets MOM6_DOMAIN_TYPE=GLOBAL and the global parameter suite
findings.what: init_args_check only asserts 'MOM6' in the compset long name, and the Case docstring gives 'G_JRA' and '1850_DATM%JRA_SLND_SICE_MOM6_SROF_SGLC_SWAV_SESP' as examples. Both lack the REGIONAL modifier. The case is then created with MOM6_DOMAIN_TYPE=GLOBAL, so the ~60 MOM_interface defaults keyed on REGIONAL are not applied. Examples: USE_KPP is unset, MAXTRUNC=0 (the run stops at the first velocity truncation), DTBT, ENERGYSAVEDAYS, the regional OBC vorticity/strain defaults, DO_GEOTHERMAL and the mixing settings. Nothing warns.
findings.trigger: A user follows the Case docstring, or passes any MOM6 compset or alias without %REGIONAL (e.g. G_JRA, C_JRA, or a hand-written long name).
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/vcg/t_nonregional.py: Case(compset='1850_DATM%NYF_SLND_SICE_MOM6_SROF_SGLC_SWAV', ...). Expected a refusal (or REGIONAL). Observed: created in 14 s; env_case COMPSET=...MOM6_SROF...; env_run MOM6_DOMAIN_TYPE=GLOBAL. The REGIONAL-keyed defaults are in components/mom/param_templates/MOM_input.yaml (e.g. USE_KPP, MAXTRUNC 'else: 0', DO_GEOTHERMAL 'else: False').
findings.root_cause: The compset validation checks for the model (MOM6) but not for the REGIONAL option, which is what selects MOM_interface's regional parameter set (config_component.xml: MOM6_DOMAIN_TYPE=REGIONAL only for compset '_MOM6%[^_]*REGIONAL'). The docstring examples predate the REGIONAL compsets.
findings.smallest_fix: In init_args_check, require re.search(r'_MOM6%[^_]*REGIONAL', compset_lname) with a message naming the CR_/GR_/CWR_/GWR_ aliases, and change the docstring examples to CR_JRA and a %REGIONAL long name.

findings.title: A second Case() with a different cesmroot in the same process reads the first CESM's compsets, grids and machines
findings.what: CIME_interface appends the new cimeroot to the end of sys.path and does 'from CIME.XML.files import Files'. Once a first CESM's CIME package is imported, every later CIME_interface(cesmroot=B) silently reuses tree A's CIME. Compsets, component config, grids, mesh paths, machines and MACHINES_SPEC_FILE all come from A, while cimeroot/srcroot (and so the create_newcase executable) point at B. Aliases only in B are refused, aliases in both resolve to A's long names, and CrocoDash's _max_tasks_per_node, get_mesh_path and get_case use A.
findings.trigger: One notebook or long-lived process (e.g. the CrocoDash MCP server, a test session) creating cases against two CESM checkouts. Example: CESM_crocodash, then CESM_wu2r05, which has CR_JRA_GLOFAS, GR_JRA_GLOFAS and the other *_GLOFAS aliases that CESM_crocodash lacks.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/vcg/t_two_roots.py: initialize(A); initialize(B). For B, cimeroot=.../CESM_wu2r05/cime, but CIME.__file__, CONFIG_CPL_FILE and MACHINES_SPEC_FILE are all under CESM_crocodash. t_two_roots_case.py after_A: 'CR_JRA_GLOFAS in cime.compsets for CESM_wu2r05 -> False', then Case(cesmroot=CESM_wu2r05, compset='CR_JRA_GLOFAS') raises 'AssertionError: compset must be a valid CESM compset long name or alias.' In a fresh process B lists CR_JRA_GLOFAS (t_roots_dump.py, CESM_wu2r05.json).
findings.root_cause: Python caches the CIME package in sys.modules after the first import; appending another root to sys.path (at the end, too) never re-imports it. Nothing checks that the imported CIME belongs to the requested cimeroot.
findings.smallest_fix: In CIME_interface.__init__, if 'CIME' is already in sys.modules and Path(CIME.__file__).resolve() is not under self.cimeroot.resolve(), raise a clear error ('visualCaseGen already loaded CIME from <A>; restart the kernel to use <B>'). Also insert the root only if it is not already on sys.path.

findings.title: Case() accepts an ocn_topo built on a different Grid than ocn_grid and writes an inconsistent case (OCN_NX/NIGLOBAL from one grid, topo/mesh/supergrid from the other)
findings.what: init_args_check only checks isinstance(ocn_topo, Topo). If the Topo was built on another grid (e.g. a cell re-run with a new resolution), OCN_NX/OCN_NY, NIGLOBAL/NJGLOBAL and the forcings use ocn_grid, while the topo file, ESMF mesh, SCRIP, CICE grid and WW3 inputs are written from the topo's own grid. Case() succeeds; the mismatch only shows up when MOM6/CMEPS start in the batch job.
findings.trigger: A notebook where the user re-creates Grid (new resolution or extent) but passes a Topo still built on the old grid.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/vcg/t_mismatch.py: gA=Grid(res=0.5) (8x8), tB=Topo(Grid(res=0.25)) (16x16); Case(ocn_grid=gA, ocn_topo=tB, ...). Expected: a refusal. Observed: 'CREATED without error'; OCN_NX=8, OCN_NY=8, NIGLOBAL=8; topo file depth (16,16); ESMF mesh elementCount=256; supergrid 16x16.
findings.root_cause: There is no consistency check between ocn_topo's grid (Topo._grid) and ocn_grid, and _create_grid_input_files writes the topo-derived files without comparing them to the grid.
findings.smallest_fix: In init_args_check: if ocn_topo.depth.shape != (ocn_grid.ny, ocn_grid.nx) (or ocn_topo._grid is not ocn_grid with differing coordinates), raise ValueError('ocn_topo was built on a different grid than ocn_grid').

findings.title: A failing case.setup is reported only as 'Error running ./case.setup.' and the caseroot holding CaseStatus/logs is then deleted
findings.what: run_case_setup runs ./case.setup with capture_output=True and, on a nonzero exit, raises RuntimeError(f'Error running {cmd}.'), discarding stdout and stderr. CrocoDash's Case() then catches the failure and _remove_failed_attempt deletes the new caseroot, so CaseStatus and every other trace of why case.setup failed are gone. Unlike create_newcase (whose stderr is now printed, vCG #25) and xmlchange (stderr in the message), this call loses the reason. It is not the double message of #21.
findings.trigger: Any case.setup failure during Case() (e.g. a PE layout or machine environment problem, or a non-local setup issue).
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/vcg/t_setup_fail.py: inside the repro, case_tools.subprocess.run is wrapped so that './case.setup' becomes "echo 'ERROR: (simulated) the real reason case.setup failed' >&2; exit 1". Expected: the error contains the reason. Observed: "RuntimeError 'Error running ./case.setup --non-local.'", __cause__ None, and 'Removing files from the failed attempt: .../cases/audit_vcg_setupfail', so the caseroot no longer exists.
findings.root_cause: run_case_setup drops runout.stdout and runout.stderr. CrocoDash's cleanup-on-failure removes the only on-disk record.
findings.smallest_fix: case_tools.run_case_setup: use text=True and raise RuntimeError(f'Error running {cmd} in {caseroot}:\n{runout.stdout[-2000:]}\n{runout.stderr}'), as xmlchange already does.

findings.title: After any failed Case() call, configure_forcings() on an earlier case crashes with KeyError('CASEROOT') or TypeError instead of the guard's message
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/vcg/t_failed_second.py: A=Case(...) OK; Case(..., atm_grid_name='T63x') raises ValueError; then A.configure_forcings(reference_ocean) gives 'TypeError: expected str, bytes or os.PathLike object, not NoneType' (pathlib). t_failed_second2.py: the second Case(cesmroot=<missing dir>) raises AssertionError; then A.configure_forcings gives KeyError('CASEROOT'). Expected: the clear RuntimeError from the guard.
findings.what: Case.__init__ re-initialises visualCaseGen's global state (initialize_visualCaseGen) before it validates its arguments. A second Case() that fails validation, or fails inside initialize, leaves cvars['CASEROOT'] at None or removes it entirely. The multi-case guard in configure_forcings (Path(cvars['CASEROOT'].value)) then raises a bare TypeError or KeyError for the earlier, valid case, instead of explaining that it can no longer be configured in this session.
findings.trigger: A notebook: create case A, run a second Case() cell with a typo (bad atm_grid_name, missing cesmroot, ...), then go back and call A.configure_forcings().
findings.root_cause: The CASEROOT guard assumes cvars always holds a CASEROOT string. A failed Case() resets cvars (ConfigVar.reboot pops every entry, and initialize runs before init_args_check) without setting it.
findings.smallest_fix: case.py:623: active = cvars['CASEROOT'].value if 'CASEROOT' in cvars else None; if active is None or Path(active) != self.caseroot: raise RuntimeError(...), with a message that also covers 'a later Case() call, even a failed one, reset visualCaseGen'. Related: #250, and #326 (1.1), which writes per caseroot.

findings.title: Custom-grid cases keep create_newcase's placeholder ROF_NX/ROF_NY (360x180 for GLOFAS) and ATM/LND_NX/NY=0
findings.what: In the xmlchange path that CrocoDash uses (add_grids_to_ccs_config=False), create_newcase runs with --res USER_RES, so ATM/LND/ROF grids start as null or the compset defaults. _update_component_grids_xml then sets ATM_GRID, LND_GRID, ROF_GRID and their DOMAIN_MESH, but not their NX/NY, which it does set for OCN/ICE/WAV. For GR_JRA/GWR_JRA/CR_JRA (DROF%GLOFAS), the case ends up with ROF_GRID=GLOFAS and the GLOFAS mesh (21,600,000 elements; ccs_config nx=7200, ny=3000) but ROF_NX=360 and ROF_NY=180 (rx1 leftovers). DROF's nx_global/ny_global come from ROF_NX/NY and are exported to the mediator, which uses them as the 2-D dims when writing rof fields to its restart (med_io: 'grid2d size not consistent' is only a log warning). GRID also keeps the stale long name 'a%null_l%null_oi%null_r%rx1_g%null_w%wgx3v7...'.
findings.trigger: Any CrocoDash case with a data runoff grid (CR_JRA, GR_JRA, GWR_JRA, CWR_JRA and the MARBL variants). ATM/LND NX/NY=0 affects every case.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/vcg/t_gwr.py: Case(compset='GWR_JRA', atm_grid_name='TL319'). env_build.xml: ROF_GRID=GLOFAS, ROF_NX=360, ROF_NY=180, ATM_NX=0, ATM_NY=0, LND_NX=0, GRID=a%null_l%null_oi%null_r%rx1_g%null_w%wgx3v7_z%null_m%null. Expected ROF_NX=7200, ROF_NY=3000 (component_grids_nuopc.xml GLOFAS) and ATM 640x320. Runtime effect (the mediator restart writes rof fields with 360x180 dims for 21.6M points; PIO's compmap bounds assert is commented out in pio_rearrange.c:2093) was NOT run.
findings.root_cause: _update_component_grids_xml copies NX/NY only for the components that share the custom ocean grid, and assumes nothing reads ATM/LND/ROF NX/NY.
findings.smallest_fix: After each ATM_GRID/LND_GRID/ROF_GRID xmlchange, also xmlchange <COMP>_NX/<COMP>_NY from self._cime.domains[comp][grid].nx/.ny (the ComponentGrid tuple already holds them).

findings.title: Case(machine=None), the documented default, always raises 'Couldn't determine machine' even when the machine was detected
findings.what: The docstring gives machine a default of None, and __init__ has self.machine = machine or self.cime.machine. But init_args_check receives the raw argument first and raises when machine is None, so the auto-detection fallback is dead code. The message claims the machine couldn't be determined although visualCaseGen detected it.
findings.trigger: Python API call without machine= (e.g. on Derecho or Casper, where CIME detects the machine).
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/vcg/t_machine.py: initialize() reports cime.machine='casper'; Case(..., machine=None) raises 'ValueError: Couldn't determine machine. Please provide the machine argument.' Expected: machine falls back to 'casper' (per case.py:178).
findings.root_cause: init_args_check(machine=machine) is called before the fallback at case.py:178 is applied.
findings.smallest_fix: Pass machine=machine or self.cime.machine to init_args_check (and keep that value for project_required).

findings.title: A grid named like a standard CESM grid is refused with advice to use override=True, which then builds a regional case that inherits that global grid's MOM6 defaults
findings.what: CrocoDash creates cases with add_grids_to_ccs_config=False, so it never registers grids in ccs_config. The check `ocn_grid.name in cime.domains['ocnice']` can therefore only fire on a clash with a standard grid name (tx2_3v2, gx1v7, tx0.25v1, T42, 4x5, ...). The message wrongly blames 'a previous case ... deleted without override=True' and tells the user to pass override=True. Doing so creates the case with OCN_GRID=<standard name>, and MOM_interface's MOM_input.yaml then selects that global grid's files and values (e.g. for tx2_3v2: KH_BG_2D file, tidal energy file, state_restore file, SeaWiFS chl, channels list, geothermal file, MAXTRUNC).
findings.trigger: Grid(name='tx2_3v2') or another standard ocnice name, then Case(..., override=True) as the error message advises.
findings.repro: Reading only: case.py:348-353 message text; cime.domains['ocnice'] lists 65 standard names (CESM_crocodash.json from t_roots_dump.py); components/mom/param_templates/MOM_input.yaml has 19 'OCN_GRID == "tx2_3v2"' entries (lines 116, 610, 661, 671, 1341, 2144, 2467, 2650, 3067, 4045, ...). Expected: a refusal saying the name is reserved by CESM, with no override escape.
findings.root_cause: The check was written for visualCaseGen's ccs_config mode (grids added to component_grids_nuopc.xml) and its message and override bypass were kept after CrocoDash switched to xmlchange mode.
findings.smallest_fix: Make the clash unconditional (ignore override) with the message 'ocn_grid name <n> is a standard CESM grid name; choose another name'.

also_noticed: visualCaseGen case_creator.py:621: _apply_ocn_grid_xmlchanges tests OCN_GRID_MODE == 'Custom', but the only options are Standard/Create New (grid_options.py:141), so the NTASKS_OCN sizing never runs (dead code; CrocoDash uses PECOUNT instead).

visualCaseGen case_creator.py:943-950: _wav_uses_custom_ocn_grid() is True for SWAV too, so stub-wave cases get WAV_GRID/WAV_NX/NY/WAV_DOMAIN_MESH set to the ocean grid (seen in the smoke and audit_vcg_relin cases); probably harmless (cosmetic).

visualCaseGen case_creator.py:517-525: create_newcase is built as an unquoted shell string (shell=True), so a caseroot/project containing spaces or shell metacharacters breaks the command (laptop paths).

Leak: every Case() calls initialize(), which leaves ~1,670 ipywidgets alive (6,731 after 4 initializes, ~5 MB RSS each; t_leak.py) and appends cimeroot to sys.path again (cime_interface.py:54); matters for long-lived processes (MCP server).

visualCaseGen cime_interface.py:122-124: the CIME version check shells out to `git describe --tags`. A cime tree with no git metadata or reachable tags gives an opaque CalledProcessError (git's stderr goes to the Jupyter server log, not the notebook; t_cimecheck.py). It is pinned to cime 6.4.x (all three local roots are cime6.4.1).

visualCaseGen cime_interface.py:859-870/761-769: expand_env_vars leaves '$ENV{SCRATCH}' literal when SCRATCH is unset (Derecho CIME_OUTPUT_ROOT=$ENV{SCRATCH}) and os.makedirs then creates a dir literally named '$ENV{SCRATCH}' in cwd; CrocoDash would use it as cime_output_root (reading only).

visualCaseGen case_creator.py:722-729: the DT heuristic assumes an 1800 s coupling interval and degree spacing from tlon/tlat ranges (OCN_LENX). Its comment says a 1-deg grid gets ~600 s, but the formula gives 7200 -> 1800 s; DT_THERM never exceeds 1800 even with OCN_NCPL=24. Conservative, no unsafe case found (t_lenx.py, t_polar_lenx.py).

CrocoDash case.py:1046-1050: _compute_pecount never returns None for a non-empty domain (ceil >= 1), so '--pecount S' is always passed, contradicting its docstring (PE-layout area, related #350/#288).

CrocoDash case.py:76/335: atm_grid_name defaults to 'TL319', so any DATM%NYF compset (T62) fails unless atm_grid_name is passed. init_args_check's message dumps hundreds of grid keys, and the friendlier 'valid options' branch at case.py:917-921 is unreachable.

CrocoDash case.py:208: the override/failed-attempt cleanup uses the LOCAL machine's CIME_OUTPUT_ROOT for a non-local case; identical on NCAR (casper is forced to /glade/derecho/scratch/$USER), may differ elsewhere.
The GRID xml long name stays 'a%null_l%null_oi%null_...' after the xmlchange grid path (cosmetic; only CIME tooling that reads GRID would be misled).
checked_ok: NYF (smoke) and GWR_JRA (t_gwr.py) cases: OCN/ICE/WAV_GRID, NX/NY, OCN/ICE/WAV_DOMAIN_MESH and MASK_MESH point at the written ESMF mesh; ATM/LND/ROF meshes resolve to inputdata paths (repro).

user_nl_mom from vCG: INPUTDIR, GRID_FILE, TOPO_FILE, ALE_COORDINATE_CONFIG file names and NIGLOBAL/NJGLOBAL match the files CrocoDash writes; NK matches the vgrid; MINIMUM/MAXIMUM_DEPTH come from the topo attrs (repro).
user_nl_cice grid_file/kmt_file match CrocoDash's ice/cice_grid_<name>_<id>.nc; WW3 *.inp copied into RUNDIR/ww3_moddef_create (GWR_JRA repro).
_coupling_interval/_set_ww3_timesteps/_set_cice_ndtd resolve $ATM_NCPL and write sane values (user_nl_ww3 dtmax=3600 = coupling interval; ndtd=1) (repro).

create_newcase command: --res USER_RES, --run-unsupported, --handle-preexisting-dirs a, --pecount, --project, --non-local when running on Casper for machine=derecho (t_relcase2 log); create_newcase now uses stdin=DEVNULL and prints stderr (the vCG #25 hang is addressed at the pin).
case_tools.xmlchange passes var=val as one argv element (no shell) and includes stderr in its error (reading).
ConfigVar.reboot/Stage.reboot/csp.reboot fully reset solver state on each initialize(); a successful second Case() is caught by the CASEROOT guard (known #250) (reading).
Antimeridian grids (xstart=178 or -182) give continuous tlon, so OCN_LENX=3.5; polar projected grids give LENX<=360 and LENY<180, within the relational constraints (t_lenx.py, t_polar_lenx.py).
CIME compatibility check passes for CESM_crocodash, CESM_wu2r05 and CESM_cdeps_years (all cime6.4.1).
ninst>1: vCG append_user_nl and CrocoDash user_nl_blocks._files both write user_nl_<model>_NNNN (reading).
MOM6_MEMORY_MODE xmlchange after case.setup is env_build (not locked at setup), so it is fine (reading + CaseStatus).
not_covered: MARBL compsets (known vCG #55) and custom long-name JRA compsets with DROF options were not created end to end (only aliases GWR_JRA and NYF long names were).

Running on Derecho itself (local, not non-local) and on the crocontainer ubuntu-latest machine; CESM_NOT_PORTED path.
