findings.title: BGCRiverNutrients converts DON and SiO3 river fluxes twice and DOP and Fe not at all (100x errors)
findings.what: The unit-conversion list in BGCRiverNutrientsConfigurator.process names don_riv_flux and dsi_riv_flux twice and leaves out dop_riv_flux and dfe_riv_flux. The x0.01 factor (nmol/cm^2/s to mmol/m^2/s) is therefore applied twice to DON and SiO3, which come out 100x too small, and never to DOP and Fe, which come out 100x too large. MOM6's MARBL_tracers.F90 reads all nine fluxes (din, don, dip, dop, dsi, dfe, dic, alk, doc) with no conversion of its own. CESM's own file, riv_nut.gnews_gnm.rJRA025_to_tx2_3v2..., stores all nine in mmol/m^2/s.
findings.trigger: Any MARBL case with DROF and global_river_nutrients_filepath (e.g. river_nutrients.GNEWS_GNM.glofas.20250916.64bit.nc), when process_forcings runs bgcrivernutrients.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/configure_process/r4_river_nutrients.py builds a synthetic source with every *_riv_flux = 1.0 nmol/cm^2/s, mocks xe.Regridder as identity, then runs BGCRiverNutrientsConfigurator.process. Observed: din/dip/dic/alk/doc = 0.01, don/dsi = 0.0001, dop/dfe = 1. Expected 0.01 for all nine. The same happens with a GREGORIAN case calendar (r4g_river_nutrients_gregorian.py).
findings.root_cause: A typo in the list: vars = ["din_riv_flux","dip_riv_flux","don_riv_flux","don_riv_flux","dsi_riv_flux","dsi_riv_flux","dic_riv_flux","alk_riv_flux","doc_riv_flux"].
findings.smallest_fix: Convert each of the nine fluxes MOM6 reads exactly once: din, dip, don, dop, dsi, dfe, dic, alk and doc (_riv_flux each). Also write units "mmol/m^2/s" instead of "mmol/cm^2/s". Open PR #297 (BGC fixes) does not touch this list.

findings.title: Tides configurator always turns on body-tide forcing for M2 only, whatever tidal_constituents says
findings.what: TidesConfigurator writes TIDES = True and a hard-coded TIDE_M2 = True, and never writes TIDE_<c> for the other constituents. With TIDES on, MOM6 (MOM_tidal_forcing.F90) applies interior astronomical forcing only for constituents whose TIDE_<c> is true, and every one defaults to false. So ["M2","S2","K1","O1"] gets interior forcing for M2 only while the open boundaries carry all four, and ["K1","O1"] gets interior M2 forcing that the boundaries don't carry. regional-mom6's own setup sets TIDE_<c> = True for each constituent (regional_mom6.py:1936-1937).
findings.trigger: configure_forcings with tides and any tidal_constituents other than exactly ["M2"]. The docs and gallery examples use ["M2","K1"], ["M2","S2"] and [M2,S2,K1,O1].
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/configure_process/r3_configure_only.py, step 1: configure_forcings(..., tidal_constituents=["K1","O1"], tpxo_*_filepath=...). Observed in user_nl_mom: TIDES = True, TIDE_M2 = True, OBC_TIDE_CONSTITUENTS = "K1, O1", and no TIDE_K1 or TIDE_O1. Expected: TIDE_K1 = True and TIDE_O1 = True, with no TIDE_M2.
findings.root_cause: A static output param UserNLConfigParam("TIDE_M2") is set to "True" in configure() instead of one TIDE_<c> per requested constituent.
findings.smallest_fix: Drop the static TIDE_M2 param. In configure(), add one UserNLConfigParam(f"TIDE_{c.upper()}") = "True" per entry of tidal_constituents (the way ConditionsConfigurator adds OBC_SEGMENT_* params), and rebuild them in deserialize. This may be related to #344 ('OBC Tide Params are Changing!', empty body).

findings.title: STOP_N counts Gregorian days for NO_LEAP products, so CESM-output cases run past their last boundary record
findings.what: configure_forcings sets CALENDAR from the product (NO_LEAP for CESM_POP_OUTPUT and CESM_MOM_OUTPUT) but computes STOP_N as the pandas (proleptic Gregorian) day difference of date_range. Each Feb 29 in the range adds a day the NO_LEAP model doesn't have, so the model stops k days after date_range[1]. The OBC data end at date_range[1], and FMS time_interp_list aborts with 'time ... is after range of list' once the model passes the last record.
findings.trigger: Conditions from CESM_POP_OUTPUT or CESM_MOM_OUTPUT with a date_range that contains Feb 29 of a leap year: e.g. ['2020-02-01','2020-03-01'] (1 extra day), or a 2000-2010 run (3 extra days).
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/configure_process/r8_noleap_stopn.py runs configure_forcings(date_range=["2020-02-01 00:00:00","2020-03-01 00:00:00"], product_name="CESM_POP_OUTPUT", function_name="get_cesm_single_variable_data"). Observed in env_run.xml: CALENDAR=NO_LEAP, STOP_N=29. Expected 28 (Feb 1 to Mar 1 is 28 noleap days); 29 noleap days end on 2020-03-02. The FMS abort comes from reading FMS time_interp.F90:821-828.
findings.root_cause: (self.date_range[1] - self.date_range[0]).days ignores self.forcing_product.calendar.
findings.smallest_fix: Count the days in the product's calendar, e.g. cftime.datetime(*end, calendar=cal.cf) - cftime.datetime(*start, calendar=cal.cf), and refuse a Feb 29 endpoint for noleap. Open PR #326 moves this line unchanged, so it stays broken on 1.1. CESM-output boundaries crash earlier today (#353), so users hit this once #353 is fixed.

findings.title: OBC chunk dates are Gregorian; a chunk bound on Feb 29 crashes REGRID for NO_LEAP products
findings.what: _make_date_pairs builds GET/REGRID chunk bounds as Python (Gregorian) datetimes, and _regrid_one_chunk slices the decoded raw data with them as strings. For a NO_LEAP product the time index is a noleap CFTimeIndex, so a chunk that starts or ends on Feb 29 raises ValueError('invalid day number ... DatetimeNoLeap(2020, 2, 29...)'). With the default regrid_step_days=30, any run that starts on Jan 1 of a leap year and runs past Feb 29 hits it, because its second chunk is Jan 31 to Feb 29. With other start dates the 7-day GET chunks pass '2020-02-29' to the CESM readers, and a Feb 28 or Feb 29 start does the same for the IC request (start + 1 day).
findings.trigger: Conditions from CESM_POP_OUTPUT or CESM_MOM_OUTPUT, date_range e.g. 2020-01-01 to 2020-03-05, then process_forcings (bc).
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/configure_process/r7_noleap_obc.py calls obc.process_obc_conditions(start_date='20200101', end_date='20200305', get_step_days=7, regrid_step_days=30) with a fake access function that writes daily noleap records. Observed: chunk 2020-01-01..01-30 regrids, then chunk [2020-01-31, 2020-02-29] raises ValueError (invalid day number for DatetimeNoLeap 2020-02-29). Expected: chunks over the product's calendar.
findings.root_cause: Chunk bounds and slice strings are not in the product's calendar (dataset_varnames['calendar'] is available but not used).
findings.smallest_fix: Build the pairs with xr.date_range(start, end, calendar=<product cf calendar>, use_cftime=True), or move a Feb 29 bound to Feb 28 / Mar 1 for noleap, and slice with dataset-calendar datetimes. Related: 1.1 item Q5/#335 (QUEUE_DETAIL: 'REGRID and IC slices are calendar-safe'). For CESM output this is hidden today behind #353.

findings.title: process_forcings resume reuses truncated files from a killed run (raw chunks, merged OBCs, IC files)
findings.what: Each skip-if-exists check accepts any file whose first 4 bytes are a netCDF signature: fetch_raw_chunk for raw chunks, _merge_boundary for ocn/forcing_obc_segment_NNN.nc, and _regrid_ic via _all_written for init_*.nc and init_*_filled.nc. All of these files are written in place. A run killed mid-write leaves a truncated file, and the rerun logs 'already exists. Skipping.' Then either REGRID dies with an anonymous 'NetCDF: HDF error', or, for a merged OBC or IC file, processing 'succeeds' and the case fails only when MOM6 reads it. A truncated classic-format file even reads back as all zeros. The BGC split and WW3 spectra steps already use temp + os.replace for this reason.
findings.trigger: process_forcings killed (OOM, walltime, Ctrl-C) while a raw chunk, a merged OBC file or an IC file is being written, then process_forcings rerun to resume, as the docs suggest.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/configure_process/r5_truncated.py halves a valid raw chunk. is_valid_netcdf returns True and fetch_raw_chunk skips it. xr.open_dataset then raises 'OSError NetCDF: HDF error' (NETCDF4), or reads 3000/3000 zeros (NETCDF3_64BIT). r5b_truncated_outputs.py halves forcing_obc_segment_001.nc: _merge_boundary logs 'Merged file ... already exists. Skipping.' Halving init_tracers_filled.nc gives _all_written(...) == True. Expected: a truncated file is rewritten or rejected.
findings.root_cause: The magic-byte check is not a completeness check, and outputs are not written atomically.
findings.smallest_fix: Write every output to '<name>.tmp' and os.replace it into place once complete. For raw chunks, fetch_raw_chunk passes a temp output_filename to the access function and renames afterwards. Optionally validate by opening the file instead of reading 4 bytes. Related: #336 (finished-step records, 1.1).

findings.title: configure_forcings deletes extract_forcings (raw downloads) on every call for cases created with override=True
findings.what: If the Case was created with override=True, as in the tutorials, every configure_forcings call rmtree's inputdir/extract_forcings, even when the configuration is unchanged and stale_outputs() found nothing stale. That removes raw_data, regridded_data and the ww3/ and cice/ staging folders. The docstring says only files made for a different configuration are removed. The next process_forcings downloads and regrids everything again, then skips MERGE because ocn/ survived. With the get_glorys_data_script_for_cli workflow, data the user downloaded by hand with the script is lost.
findings.trigger: Case(..., override=True), then configure_forcings and process_forcings, then configure_forcings again with the same arguments (a notebook cell rerun, or adding tides), then process_forcings.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/configure_process/r2_reconfigure.py with the 'override' argument: after an identical second configure_forcings, only config.json is left under extract_forcings, raw north_unprocessed.2020-01-01_2020-01-03.nc is gone, and process_forcings fetches it again (mtime changed). With 'nooverride', all raw and regridded files are kept and nothing is fetched again.
findings.root_cause: A pre-#294 override wipe was kept after #294 added stale_outputs(), so the creation-time override flag is applied again on every configure.
findings.smallest_fix: Delete the `if self.override is True and self.extract_forcings_path.exists(): shutil.rmtree(...)` lines. Case(override=True) already wipes inputdir at creation, and stale_outputs() handles changed configurations.

findings.title: configure_forcings accepts a date_range whose end is not after its start: negative STOP_N, then a misleading 'no output' error
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/configure_process/r3_configure_only.py, step 2: date_range=["2020-01-05 00:00:00","2020-01-01 00:00:00"]. configure succeeds and env_run.xml gets STOP_N=-4. process_forcings then raises FileNotFoundError 'No files for [south] — preceding phase produced no output.' Step 3, with the same start and end, gives STOP_N=0 and is accepted. Expected: a ValueError at configure naming date_range.
findings.what: configure_forcings checks only that date_range holds two strings. An end before or equal to the start is written to the case as STOP_N=-4 or STOP_N=0. process_forcings then fails in the OBC coverage check with an error that says nothing about the dates.
findings.trigger: A swapped date_range, or the same day for start and end.
findings.root_cause: There is no ordering check after pd.to_datetime(date_range).
findings.smallest_fix: After self.date_range = pd.to_datetime(date_range): `if self.date_range[1] <= self.date_range[0]: raise ValueError('date_range end must be after its start')`.

findings.title: tidal_constituents given as a string is split into characters: OBC_TIDE_CONSTITUENTS = "M, 2"
findings.what: The configure_forcings docstring promises a TypeError when tidal_constituents is not a list of strings, but TidesConfigurator has no validate_args. A string such as "M2" is iterated character by character, giving OBC_TIDE_N_CONSTITUENTS = 2 and OBC_TIDE_CONSTITUENTS = "M, 2" in user_nl_mom. The error only shows up later, in the TPXO lookup at process time or in MOM6 at run time.
findings.trigger: configure_forcings(..., tidal_constituents="M2", tpxo_elevation_filepath=..., tpxo_velocity_filepath=...).
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/configure_process/r11_tides_string.py: configure succeeds, and user_nl_mom has OBC_TIDE_N_CONSTITUENTS = 2 and OBC_TIDE_CONSTITUENTS = "M, 2". Expected a TypeError.
findings.root_cause: TidesConfigurator never validates its inputs, and configure() uses len() and join() on whatever it is given.
findings.smallest_fix: Add TidesConfigurator.validate_args: tidal_constituents must be a non-empty list of distinct str, normalized to upper case.

verify:mom6_forge-a3.verdict_reason: The code does what the finding says, and my own minimal repro reproduces it both standalone and through a CrocoDash Case. The reloaded Topo has min_depth 0.0 instead of the saved 10.0. Cells shallower than the saved min_depth become ocean in tmask, masked_depth and the written topog, and Case passes MINIMUM_DEPTH = 0.0 to MOM6. No guard prevents it. The mom6_forge test (tests/test_topo.py:8, fixture tests/conftest.py:352) misses the bug because its fixture uses min_depth=0. from_version_control is a public, documented constructor (docs/source/widgets.md:230) and is re-exported through CrocoDash.topo. Nothing in TRIAGE.md, QUEUE.md, the open issue and PR lists, or a gh search of mom6_forge issues and PRs (all states) for "from_version_control" covers it.
verify:mom6_forge-a3.title: Topo.from_version_control reloads every version-controlled bathymetry with min_depth=0.0, so cells shallower than the saved min_depth become ocean
verify:mom6_forge-a3.what: from_version_control builds a placeholder Topo(grid, 0.0, git=True). Topo.__init__ sets self._min_depth = 0.0 first and then commits MinDepthEditCommand(new_value=0.0) to the existing git history. MinDepthEditCommand.__call__ records old_value as the current value, so the commit stores old=0.0 and new=0.0. reapply_changes() replays the saved history and then this new command last. tcm.undo() then reverses it with old_value 0.0, so min_depth stays 0.0. The code comment at topo.py:288 says the undo leaves the correct min_depth, but it does not. As a result tmask, masked_depth, the written topog depth and its min_depth attribute are all computed against 0 instead of the saved min_depth. CrocoDash Case also passes minimum_depth=ocn_topo.min_depth, so the case gets MINIMUM_DEPTH = 0.0. Each reload also adds two commits (COMMAND + UNDO) to the bathymetry's history and leaves the min_depth=0 command on the redo stack. Raw depth is reloaded correctly. A min_depth changed later in TopoEditor is lost the same way.
verify:mom6_forge-a3.trigger: Build a bathymetry with version control (Topo(..., git=True), as TopoEditor requires) and a nonzero min_depth. In a later session, reload it with Topo.from_version_control(domain_dir), which is the documented way back to an edited bathymetry, then write it or pass it to a CrocoDash Case.
verify:mom6_forge-a3.repro_command: source .../scratchpad/audit/env.sh; cd /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/verify/mom6_forge-a3 && timeout 900 $PY -u repro.py   (and case_repro.py for the Case path). Key lines: grid = Grid(lenx=4.0, leny=3.0, resolution=1.0, xstart=-60.0, ystart=30.0, name="a3"); topo = Topo(grid, min_depth=10.0, version_control_dir=lib, git=True); d = np.full((ny,nx),500.); d[0,:] = 5.0; topo.depth = d; re = Topo.from_version_control(topo.domain_dir); print(re.min_depth, re.tmask.sum()). case_repro.py passes the reloaded Topo to Case(..., compset 1850_DATM%NYF_..., override=True) and reads the inputdir topog and user_nl_mom.
verify:mom6_forge-a3.expected: The reloaded Topo has min_depth=10.0 and the same 8 ocean cells as the original. Row 0 (5 m) stays land with depth 0 in the topog, and MINIMUM_DEPTH = 10.0 in the case. Loading does not change the git history.

ORIGINAL : min_depth= 10.0  ocean cells= 8  masked_depth row0= [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
RELOADED : min_depth= 0.0  ocean cells= 12  masked_depth row0= [5.0, 5.0, 5.0, 5.0]
raw depth equal: True
git commits before/after reload: 2 4   (newest: "UNDO-a90eed99...", "COMMAND-Min Depth Edit")
written topog depth row0: [5.0, 5.0, 5.0, 5.0]
RELOAD#2 : min_depth= 0.0  commits= 6
Case path: inputdir ocean_topog_a3c_7ebd5a.nc attr min_depth= 0.0 depth row0= [5.0, 5.0, 5.0, 5.0]; user_nl_mom line 56: MINIMUM_DEPTH = 0.0
verify:mom6_forge-a3.root_cause: The placeholder MinDepthEditCommand that Topo.__init__ commits during from_version_control has old_value captured at construction time. That value is the placeholder 0.0, not the min_depth the replay restores, because __init__ assigns self._min_depth = min_depth before running the command. Replay applies the placeholder command last, and undoing it restores its old_value of 0.0. The undo cannot recover the replayed min_depth, contrary to the comment at topo.py:288.
verify:mom6_forge-a3.smallest_fix: In from_version_control, swap the two calls: undo the placeholder command first, then replay (topo.tcm.undo(); topo.tcm.reapply_changes()). The undone placeholder is skipped during replay, so the saved min_depth wins. I verified this by monkeypatching it in repro.py: min_depth=10.0 and 8 ocean cells. A cleaner fix is to not commit the placeholder at all when the domain already has a history (for example, a flag on __init__ that makes from_version_control apply it with skip_version_control=True) and drop the undo. That also stops the two extra commits per load and the stale redo entry. Also change the test fixture get_rect_topo_with_vc (tests/conftest.py:352) to a nonzero min_depth so test_topo_from_version_control catches this.
verify:mom6_forge-a3.fixed_on_main: No. origin/main 83d7692 has the same from_version_control (topo.py:283-293 there); the only change is Grid.from_supergrid -> Grid.from_supergrid_file. Neither #126 nor #155 touches MinDepthEditCommand or TopoCommandManager.undo, so a pin bump would not fix it.
verify:mom6_forge-a3.related: none (no matching issue or PR in NCAR/mom6_forge in any state; not in TRIAGE.md or QUEUE.md). The existing test test_topo_from_version_control (tests/test_topo.py:8) misses it because its fixture uses min_depth=0.

findings.title: Case() fails with "Path <dir> doesn't exist" when the parent of caseroot or inputdir is missing; CrocoDash's own parent mkdirs are dead code
findings.what: Case() raises RuntimeError "Case configuration failed: Path <parent> doesn't exist" whenever the parent directory of inputdir or of caseroot does not exist yet. The inputdir.mkdir(parents=True) at case.py:383 and the caseroot.parent.mkdir at case.py:476-477 are meant to create those parents, but they are never reached. The same check also rejects a bare or './' relative caseroot ('Path  doesn't exist', with an empty path) and any '~/...' path ('Path ~ doesn't exist').
findings.trigger: Any Case() call, `crocodash create`, or MCP create_case where the case or input folder is new. One example is the gallery starter_case.yaml (`inputdir: <inputdir>/my_case`) pointed at a scratch subfolder that does not exist yet.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/creation_cli/r1_missing_parent.py (log r1.log). Case(caseroot=<existing>/audit_ccl_r1a, inputdir=<D>/missing_parent_a/sub/audit_ccl_r1a) raised 'RuntimeError: Case configuration failed: Path .../missing_parent_a/sub doesn't exist' from filechooser.py:400 via _validate_value (filechooser.py:189). A missing caseroot parent gave the same error for .../missing_parent_b/sub. Nothing was left on disk. After mkdir of the parent, a retry in the same process succeeded. r2b_relcase.py: caseroot='audit_x' or './audit_x' gave 'Path  doesn't exist', and '~/audit_x' gave 'Path ~ doesn't exist'. Expected: CrocoDash creates the parents (as the code at case.py:383/476 intends) and the case is made.
findings.root_cause: _configure_case (case.py:197) runs before the directories are created. It sets cvars['CUSTOM_GRID_PATH'] = inputdir (case.py:903) and cvars['CASEROOT'] = caseroot (case.py:1060). ConfigVar pushes each value into visualCaseGen's FileChooser widgets (grid_widgets.py:53 and launcher_widgets.py:23, both new_only=True). FileChooser's @validate('value') (filechooser.py:183-189) calls _check_selection, which raises RuntimeError when os.path.exists(parent) is False (filechooser.py:399-400). The error is wrapped at case.py:202-203. The parent mkdirs at case.py:383 and 476-477 run only after that, so they are unreachable for a missing parent.
findings.smallest_fix: CrocoDash: in Case.__init__, after init_args_check and before _configure_case, resolve the paths and create the parents: Path(inputdir).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) and the same for caseroot. Then drop the dead mkdir at case.py:476-477. visualCaseGen's widget check is correct for the GUI, so CrocoDash should own the fix.

findings.title: Relative inputdir is written as a relative path into user_nl_mom INPUTDIR, OCN/ICE/WAV_DOMAIN_MESH, MASK_MESH and the case state
findings.what: Case(inputdir='inputs_rel/x') creates the case and reports success. The case is configured with cwd-relative paths: INPUTDIR = inputs_rel/x/ocn in user_nl_mom, and OCN_DOMAIN_MESH/MASK_MESH = inputs_rel/x/ocn/ESMF_mesh_*.nc in env xml. _crocodash_state.json stores inputdir and the grid paths as relative. The model reads these from RUNDIR, and later CrocoDash calls from another cwd cannot find the files.
findings.trigger: A notebook or script that passes a relative inputdir (for example inputdir='input/mycase'), or a YAML recipe with a relative inputdir.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/creation_cli/r2a_relinput.py (log r2a.log): cwd=<D>/relwd, absolute caseroot, inputdir='inputs_rel/audit_ccl_r2a'. Observed: STATE inputdir 'inputs_rel/audit_ccl_r2a'; user_nl_mom 'INPUTDIR = inputs_rel/audit_ccl_r2a/ocn'; env xml OCN_DOMAIN_MESH and MASK_MESH relative. After os.chdir elsewhere, case.process_forcings() raised FileNotFoundError: 'inputs_rel/audit_ccl_r2a/extract_forcings/config.json'. Expected: absolute paths everywhere.
findings.root_cause: Case.__init__ stores Path(inputdir) without .resolve() (case.py:171). That value is passed unchanged to CUSTOM_GRID_PATH (case.py:903), which visualCaseGen writes into user_nl_mom and the mesh xmlchanges, and into the state file (case.py:1078) and config.json.
findings.smallest_fix: At the top of Case.__init__, set caseroot/inputdir/cesmroot = Path(x).expanduser().resolve() before init_args_check and _configure_case. The same line also fixes the relative-caseroot and '~' issues.

findings.title: Relative caseroot with a folder part creates the case under $HOME, then Case() crashes and leaves the half-made case behind
findings.what: With caseroot='cases_rel/mycase', CrocoDash's checks run against cwd. visualCaseGen's CaseCreator then rewrites a relative caseroot as Path.home()/caseroot and runs create_newcase there. The following xmlchange/case.setup calls use the cwd-relative CASEROOT and fail. Cleanup removes the inputdir but not the case under $HOME. If ~/cases_rel does not exist, the error is the misleading 'Cannot write to /home/<user>/cases_rel/mycase'. '~' is never expanded in cesmroot, caseroot or inputdir, so cesmroot='~/...' fails with 'Given CESM root directory doesn't exist!'.
findings.trigger: Case(caseroot='cases/mycase', ...) from a notebook whose cwd is not $HOME, or a YAML recipe with a relative caseroot or with '~'.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/creation_cli/r2d_relsub.py, run with HOME=<D>/fakehome and cwd=<D>/relwd3 (log r2d.log). create_newcase ran with --case <fakehome>/cases_rel/audit_ccl_r2d. Case() then raised 'RuntimeError: Error running ./xmlchange OCN_GRID=ccr2d --non-local in cases_rel/audit_ccl_r2d: [Errno 2] No such file or directory'. The cwd case does not exist, and fakehome/cases_rel/audit_ccl_r2d remains as a half-made case. r2.log: without ~/cases_rel the error was 'Cannot write to /glade/u/home/manishrv/cases_rel/audit_ccl_r2'.
findings.root_cause: CrocoDash never resolves caseroot (case.py:170, and cvars CASEROOT at case.py:1060). visualCaseGen resolves a relative caseroot against Path.home() only for create_newcase (case_creator.py:123-125). Its xmlchange/run_case_setup use cwd=CASEROOT as given (case_tools.py:34/144), so the two halves see different directories.
findings.smallest_fix: Use the same fix as the relative-inputdir finding: Path(caseroot).expanduser().resolve() (and the same for inputdir and cesmroot) at the top of Case.__init__. visualCaseGen: replace Path.home()/caseroot with caseroot.resolve() at case_creator.py:124-125.

findings.title: crocodash duplicate / fork always run with override=True and silently delete existing dirs, including the source case's bld/run dir when the case name is reused
findings.what: duplicate_case() and ForkBundle.fork() pass override=True to create_case_from_yaml. The CLI has no flag to turn this off. Case() then rmtree's the new inputdir, the new caseroot and CIME_OUTPUT_ROOT/<new case name> with no prompt. Duplicating /A/mycase to /B/mycase therefore deletes the source case's bld/run dir, which holds its model output and restarts. A --inputdir that is an existing folder, such as the one holding the source case's inputdir, is deleted whole.
findings.trigger: `crocodash duplicate --source /A/mycase --case /B/mycase --inputdir <existing folder>`, `crocodash fork` with the same case name, or the MCP duplicate_case_tool / fork_case.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/creation_cli/r7_dup_override.py (log r7.log). CrocoDash.case._remove_previous was monkeypatched to log and stop instead of deleting. duplicate_case(<D>/cases4/audit_ccl_r4a, <D>/cases7/audit_ccl_r4a, <D>/inputs4) would rmtree <D>/inputs4 (the folder holding the SOURCE inputdir, exists=True) and /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/audit_ccl_r4a (the SOURCE case's bld/run dir, exists=True). Expected: refuse when a target exists or when the new name equals the source name, unless the user asks for override.
findings.root_cause: override=True is hard-coded in duplicate_case (shareable.py:402) and fork (shareable.py:553). Case.__init__ with override=True removes CIME_OUTPUT_ROOT/<caseroot.name> by name (case.py:208-212), whichever case owns it.
findings.smallest_fix: Pass override=False in duplicate_case and fork, or expose --override on the CLI defaulting to False. Also refuse when Path(new_caseroot).name == source caseroot name.

findings.title: Bundling or duplicating a case crashes with KeyError when it has user_nl settings in a component or parameter block that the reference case leaves empty
findings.what: CaseBundle.diff() indexes other_case.user_nl_objs[key][subkey] for every module in the source case's user_nl files. A module the freshly made reference case lacks raises KeyError. That includes 'Global' for an empty user_nl_cpl/user_nl_datm/user_nl_drof, and any MOM block such as KPP%. So bundle, duplicate and identify_non_standard_case_info all crash for these common edits.
findings.trigger: Add any line to user_nl_cpl (or user_nl_datm/drof), or a MOM block parameter (KPP%...%KPP), then run `crocodash bundle`, `crocodash duplicate`, or the MCP bundle_case.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/creation_cli/r6_bundle_diff.py cpl|kpp (logs r6a.log, r6b.log; MOM_RPS dir added to PYTHONPATH, which is the known env artifact). Appending 'orb_iyear = 1990' to user_nl_cpl gave 'KeyError: Global' at shareable.py:248 in diff. Appending 'KPP%\nN_SMOOTH = 2\n%KPP' to user_nl_mom gave 'KeyError: KPP'. Expected: the parameters are reported as non-standard and carried over.
findings.root_cause: diff() assumes each module present in the source is also present in the reference (`other_case.user_nl_objs[key][subkey]`). The MOM param reader only creates a module key when the file has a parameter in it.
findings.smallest_fix: Use other_case.user_nl_objs.get(key, {}).get(subkey, {}) in diff(). Also carry the block name, so that copy_user_nl_params_from_case can write KPP% params back inside their block.

findings.title: duplicate/fork replay xmlchanges with the trailing '--non-local' flag inside the value and crash after the new case is half made
findings.what: apply_xmlchanges_to_case splits each replay.sh line './xmlchange DOUT_S=FALSE --non-local' at '=' and passes 'FALSE --non-local' as the value. CIME rejects it ('Entry DOUT_S was listed as type logical but had val 'FALSE --non-local''). duplicate_case raises only after the new case has been created and its files copied, so the new case is left without the remaining changes.
findings.trigger: A case created or edited non-locally, such as a derecho case made from Casper (this sandbox). Every xmlchange in its replay.sh carries --non-local. Any user xmlchange (DOUT_S, JOB_PRIORITY, ...) is then flagged non-standard, and `crocodash duplicate` or `crocodash fork` with plan xmlchanges=true replays it. Other flags (--file, --append, -N) break the same way.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/creation_cli/r5_duplicate.py (log r5.log): xmlchange('DOUT_S','FALSE', is_non_local=True) on the source, then duplicate_case(A, B, IB). Observed: 'RuntimeError: Error running ./xmlchange 'DOUT_S=FALSE --non-local' --non-local in .../audit_ccl_r5b: ERROR: Entry DOUT_S was listed as type logical but had val 'FALSE --non-local''. Case B exists, half configured. Expected: DOUT_S=FALSE applied.
findings.root_cause: replay.sh lines are parsed with str.split instead of CIME's argument syntax. Flags after the setting become part of the value (shareable.py:101-102), and _read_xmlchanges does the same at shareable.py:192-196.
findings.smallest_fix: Parse each line with shlex.split, drop tokens that start with '-', and split the remaining 'K=V[,K2=V2]' token on commas and '='. Validate everything before creating the new case.

findings.title: duplicate/fork/bundle drop the user's changed values for any parameter CrocoDash also writes (e.g. DT in user_nl_mom, STOP_N)
findings.what: CaseBundle.diff compares only parameter or xml names against the reference case, never values. A parameter the reference also sets is treated as standard, and the duplicate silently gets the CrocoDash default back. Examples are a hand-edited DT or DT_THERM, MINIMUM_DEPTH, OBC_* nudging, or an xml variable such as STOP_N/RUN_STARTDATE/NTASKS. bundle() records nothing about it either.
findings.trigger: Edit DT = 1800.0 to DT = 900.0 in user_nl_mom (e.g. after a CFL crash), then `crocodash duplicate` or `crocodash bundle` + `crocodash fork`.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/creation_cli/r5_duplicate.py: source user_nl_mom has 'DT = 900.0', duplicate cases5/audit_ccl_r5b has 'DT = 1800.0'. No warning was given, and non_standard_case_info lists no DT. STOP_N=1 on the source was likewise not carried. Expected: DT = 900.0 in the duplicate.
findings.root_cause: diff() tests `subsubkey not in other_case.user_nl_objs[key][subkey]` and `k not in other_case.xmlchanges`, which is name membership only. copy_user_nl_params_from_case/apply_xmlchanges_to_case only replay those names.
findings.smallest_fix: In diff(), also flag a parameter whose value differs from the reference (compare ['value'] for user_nl, and the last value per key for xmlchanges). Replay it after the reference values, replacing the reference line rather than appending a duplicate key.

findings.title: fork drops the bundled runoff map (mapping/) and CICE forcing (ice/), duplicate drops mapping/, and validate_case reports nothing
findings.what: CaseBundle.bundle() copies each configurator's outputs keeping their layout under inputdir (mapping/<map>.nc, ice/cice_forcing.nc). ForkBundle.fork() copies only bundle/wav and bundle/ocn into the new inputdir, so the runoff map and the CICE restoring file are silently left out. duplicate_case copies ocn/ice/wav but not mapping/. The forked case's ROF2OCN_*_RMAPNAME points at a map that does not exist, and fork's validate_case() says nothing. The base validate_output_filepaths only checks paths that get_output_filepaths already filtered to existing files, so it is always True.
findings.trigger: A DROF (GLOFAS) or CICE-restoring case, e.g. GR_JRA. `crocodash bundle`, then `crocodash fork`, or `crocodash duplicate`. Regenerating the GLOFAS map needs a ~200 GB PBS job.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/creation_cli/r10_fork_files.py (log r10.log). A GR_JRA case was configured with stand-in output files, then bundled and forked with plan={}. The bundle contains 'ice/cice_forcing.nc' and 'mapping/GLOFAS_to_ccr10_map_r200_f400_nnsm.nc'. In the fork: 'FORK expects map: .../inputs10/audit_ccl_r10f/mapping/GLOFAS_to_ccr10_map_r200_f400_nnsm.nc exists: False' and 'FORK ice/cice_forcing.nc exists: False', with no 'not valid yet' message. Expected: every bundled subfolder restored, or a clear missing-file report.
findings.root_cause: fork hard-codes the two subfolders wav and ocn (shareable.py:556-565), and duplicate_case hard-codes (ocn, ice, wav) (shareable.py:407). BaseConfigurator.get_output_filepaths returns only paths that exist (base.py:871-873), so validate_output_filepaths (base.py:876-881) can never fail.
findings.smallest_fix: In fork, copytree every bundle subfolder except xml_files/SourceMods into the new inputdir (dirs_exist_ok=True). In duplicate_case, add 'mapping'. Make validate_output_filepaths check the configured output paths without the exists filter.

findings.title: YAML recipes (crocodash create) silently ignore misspelled or unknown forcings keys, so tides are dropped and boundaries fall back to the defaults
findings.what: A forcings section with 'tidal_constituent: [M2, S2]' and 'boundary: [north]' creates and configures the case with exit code 0. No tides configurator is activated, and all four default boundaries are used. The only trace is an INFO line '[SKIP] tides missing args'. validate_config_structure checks only the correctly spelled tidal_constituents. configure_forcings(**kwargs) keeps only kwargs that match some configurator's constructor and drops the rest.
findings.trigger: `crocodash create --config case.yaml` (or configure_forcings from Python) with a typo in an optional forcing key: tidal_constituent, boundary, chl_processed_file, rmax without fold, etc.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/creation_cli/r12.yaml via `crocodash create --config r12.yaml --configure-only` (log r12.log): rc=0. config.json entries ['streamyears','conditions'] (no tides), and boundaries ['south','north','west','east'] although the YAML asked for [north]. Expected: an error naming the unknown keys.
findings.root_cause: There is no unknown-key check in recipe.validate_config_structure. ForcingConfigRegistry.instantiate_configurator (base.py:259-262) silently filters inputs to constructor args, and optional configurators that miss an arg are only INFO-logged as skipped.
findings.smallest_fix: In configure_forcings (or recipe.load_config), raise on any key that is not a constructor arg of a registered configurator or a configure_forcings parameter. The related 1.1 item #330 (Q9) adds an unknown-kwarg warning; 1.0.x users still hit this on main.

findings.title: dump/duplicate/bundle/fork recreate a case from compset_lname instead of the alias it was made with, so MARBL alias cases cannot be reproduced
findings.what: The state file drops the compset argument (INIT_ARGS_EXCLUDE) and keeps only compset_lname. case_to_yaml therefore always emits the long name. A case created from a standard alias (CR1850MARBL_JRA, GR1850MARBL_JRA, CWR1850MARBL_JRA...) is recreated through _configure_custom_compset, which fails on the two MOM6 modifiers (visualCaseGen #55). Every sharing flow fails for those cases, including the temp reference case that bundle builds, even though the original creation worked.
findings.trigger: Case(compset='CR1850MARBL_JRA', ...), then `crocodash dump` + `crocodash create`, or `crocodash bundle` / `duplicate` / `fork`.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/creation_cli/r8_marbl_alias.py (log r8.log). The alias case was CREATED, and its state has compset_lname only ('compset' in state: False). The same case from the lname, which is what case_to_yaml emits, FAILED: 'Case configuration failed: Invalid assignment of COMPSET_LNAME to ...MOM6%REGIONAL%MARBL-BIO_DROF_SGLC_SWAV'. Expected: the dump reproduces the case.
findings.root_cause: 'compset' is in case_state.INIT_ARGS_EXCLUDE, and recipe.case_to_yaml writes state['compset_lname'] as case.compset. The custom-compset path cannot take multi-modifier long names (visualCaseGen #55, CrocoDash #279).
findings.smallest_fix: Store the compset argument as given (alias when it was an alias) in the state, and have case_to_yaml emit it, falling back to compset_lname. Related: visualCaseGen #55 and CrocoDash #279; this stops mattering once #55 is fixed.

findings.title: _compute_pecount can never return None or pick XS, so every domain gets at least the 2-node S tier (128 ocean ranks for a 64-cell test domain)
findings.what: nodes_needed = ceil(ocean_pts / (pts_per_core*MAX_TASKS_PER_NODE)) is at least 1 for any non-empty domain, so the documented 'return None when the domain fits the default layout' branch is unreachable. A tiny domain gets pecount S: NTASKS_OCN=128 on a dedicated second node, plus 128 tasks for DATM/CPL on node 0. MOM_interface's 1-node XS tier is never requested. Leaving pecount unset is no better: CIME then defaults to M (384 OCN tasks). An 8x8 test domain cannot give each of 128 ranks a cell, so MOM6 is expected to abort at decomposition (run not attempted here).
findings.trigger: Any small Case() without ntasks_ocn, such as CLAUDE.md's 10x10 NYF quick case or the tutorials' small domains on derecho.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/creation_cli/r9_two_cases.py (log r9.log). For 64 ocean points: 'X pecount -> S NTASKS_OCN 128'. replay.sh shows --pecount S. env_mach_pes.xml of the NYF case cases1/... has OCN=128. With _compute_pecount patched to return None: NTASKS_OCN 384 (CIME default M). Expected: a 1-node layout (XS) for domains that fit on one core or one node.
findings.root_cause: math.ceil makes nodes_needed >= 1, so `if nodes_needed < 1: return None` (case.py:1047) is dead. There is also no mapping to MOM_interface's XS tier, which is only chosen when pecount XS is passed explicitly.
findings.smallest_fix: Return 'XS' when the ocean points fit a single core's share (e.g. ocean_pts <= pts_per_core) and remove the dead branch. Related: #350 (1.1 PE layout) replaces this; #288 is its duplicate; TRIAGE item 2 is the ntasks_ocn path.

findings.title: machine=None (documented default) always fails with "Couldn't determine machine" even when CIME detected the machine
findings.what: init_args_check receives the raw machine argument, not `machine or self.cime.machine`. Omitting machine therefore always raises ValueError("Couldn't determine machine. Please provide the machine argument."), and the fallback at case.py:178 is dead. The error claims detection failed when it never ran (cime.machine was 'casper' here).
findings.trigger: Case(...) without machine= on any CIME-ported host (Casper, Derecho).
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/creation_cli/r11_override.py (log r11.log): 'machine=None FAILED: ValueError Couldn't determine machine.' while visualCaseGen initialize(CESMROOT).machine == 'casper'. Expected: machine defaults to casper, or the parameter is documented as required.
findings.root_cause: case.py:160 passes `machine=machine` to init_args_check. The resolved value `machine or self.cime.machine` is computed later, at case.py:178.
findings.smallest_fix: Pass machine=machine or self.cime.machine to init_args_check (and use the same value for project_required).

findings.title: Every bundle/duplicate leaks a temp case's bld/run dir under CIME_OUTPUT_ROOT
findings.what: identify_non_standard_case_info builds a reference case in a TemporaryDirectory, which removes only the caseroot. CIME_OUTPUT_ROOT/temp_case-<uuid>/{bld,run} made by case.setup stays behind each time. That covers every `crocodash bundle`, every `crocodash duplicate`, and the MCP bundle_case.
findings.trigger: Any `crocodash bundle` or `crocodash duplicate` (or CaseBundle(...).identify_non_standard_case_info).
findings.repro: After r5/r6a/r6b/r7/r10 under /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/creation_cli/, six dirs /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/temp_case-<uuid>/{bld,run} remain (e.g. temp_case-50f034f6b74940ea8118519f80706b09, 129K, created 09:44 by r5). verify:mom6_forge-a4.verdict_reason: Reproduced independently on the pinned mom6_forge (d74c851) through the public, documented Grid.from_center API, which CrocoDash re-exports as CrocoDash.grid.Grid. With angle_deg=±90/270, small (estuary-scale) domains fail with AssertionError 'cyclic_x is only supported for 360 degree domains', and at the equator domains of any size fail. The supergrid's first and last columns hold nearly identical longitudes (max diff 2.8e-3 deg) at latitudes 0.9 deg apart, and the longitude-only rtol=1e-5 check accepts that. Nothing upstream guards against it. It is not in TRIAGE.md, QUEUE.md, or the issue/PR lists. mom6_forge PR #153, issue #132 and CrocoDash #339 cover cyclic bounding boxes and WW3 on genuinely cyclic grids, not misdetection. One correction to the finder: the bug only fires when meridian convergence across the domain stays below rtol*normalized_lon. So 'angle ±90 crashes' holds for small domains, any domain at the equator, and western-hemisphere longitudes (larger tolerance), not for every ±90 grid. Large mid-latitude ±90 domains build fine. The downstream 'wrong result' paths the finder lists (to_esmf_mesh, WW3 SMPL closure, get_bounding_boxes) cannot be reached through a Grid, because Grid construction from such a supergrid always asserts first. Only raw SupergridBase users would see them.
verify:mom6_forge-a4.title: Grid.from_center with angle_deg=±90 fails for small or equatorial domains: the rotated grid is taken for a cyclic one ("cyclic_x is only supported for 360 degree domains")

verify:mom6_forge-a4.what: Grid.is_cyclic_x and SupergridBase.is_cyclic_x decide that a grid is periodic in x when the longitudes of supergrid columns 0 and -1 match within rtol=1e-5 (np.allclose on normalize_deg(lon)). They never compare latitudes, and they use a relative tolerance on a longitude, so the tolerance is about 3.6e-3 deg near 360E and close to 0 near 0E. A grid rotated 90 deg (or -90/270) has i running north-south, so its first and last columns span almost the same longitudes at different latitudes. For small domains, and for any domain at the equator, the difference falls inside the tolerance. Grid.from_supergrid_ds then passes cyclic_x=True to Grid(), and the 'lenx == 360' assertion stops grid creation. The user never asked for a cyclic grid, so the error message is misleading too. The same path is reached through the GridCreator widget's 'From Center' mode, which prints 'Failed to create grid from centre: cyclic_x is only supported for 360 degree domains.', and through Grid.from_supergrid on any hgrid file whose i axis runs north-south.
verify:mom6_forge-a4.trigger: Creating an estuary- or coast-aligned regional grid with a quarter-turn rotation, which is the use case the from_center docstring and quickstart.md describe: Grid.from_center(lat, lon, width_m, height_m, res_m, angle_deg=90) (also -90 or 270). Examples that fail: Chesapeake mouth (37, -76, 40 km x 20 km, 2 km), Delaware (39, -75, 30x20 km, 1.5 km), Rio de la Plata (-35, -57, 40x20 km), Ganges (21, 89, 40x20 km), and Amazon (0, -50, 200x100 km; at the equator every size fails). angle_deg=0, 89, 89.9 and 180 work, and larger mid-latitude ±90 domains, e.g. (45, -70, 200x100 km), happen to escape.

verify:mom6_forge-a4.root_cause: The cyclic test is np.allclose(normalize_deg(x[:,0]), normalize_deg(x[:,-1]), rtol=1e-5). It checks only longitude, ignores latitude, and uses a relative tolerance on longitude, which gives a 1e-5*lon tolerance of up to 3.6e-3 deg near 360E. So any grid whose first and last i-columns sweep the same longitudes counts as periodic, e.g. a 90-deg-rotated or transposed grid. That includes a from_center domain rotated by ±90 deg when meridian convergence across it is below the tolerance. from_supergrid_ds trusts this flag for cyclic_x, and Grid.__init__ rejects cyclic_x when lenx != 360.
verify:mom6_forge-a4.smallest_fix: Make both Grid.is_cyclic_x (grid.py:392-406) and SupergridBase.is_cyclic_x (_supergrid.py:37-43) require matching latitudes and use an absolute tolerance on the wrapped longitude difference. For example: dlon = (x[:,0] - x[:,-1] + 180) % 360 - 180; return np.all(np.abs(dlon) < atol) and np.allclose(y[:,0], y[:,-1], rtol=0, atol=atol), with atol of about 1e-6 deg. Monkeypatched this way, both rotated cases build with cyclic_x=False, a global 360-deg Grid still round-trips through from_supergrid_ds with cyclic_x=True, and a plain 4x2-deg regional grid stays non-cyclic. A follow-up test would be from_center(..., angle_deg=90) on a small domain.

verify:mom6_forge-a2.verdict_reason: The swap at utils.py:224-225 fires when the first mesh row changes latitude more than eastward longitude. It replaces the connectivity-derived nx, which is the row stride that every caller's C-order reshape needs. I reproduced it three ways: (1) on the meshes directly; (2) through gen_rof_maps; (3) end to end through a CrocoDash Case (DROF%JRA compset, rotated from_center grid, configure_forcings, then process_forcings with runoff only). In the Case run, the generated ROF2OCN map sends runoff to interior cells, and the suggested rmax collapses from 20 km to 1 km. A monkeypatched get_mesh_dimensions that keeps the connectivity nx restores coast-only mapping. It also reproduces on offset Arctic polar-stereographic grids (from_projection EPSG:3995), not only on from_center. Not in TRIAGE.md, QUEUE.md, the baseline notes, or the open issue/PR lists of the four repos. mom6_forge #145 (haversine dx/dy) touches a different function.
verify:mom6_forge-a2.title: get_mesh_dimensions swaps nx/ny on rotated or polar-offset grids, so runoff maps send river water to interior ocean cells and Grid/Topo.from_esmf_mesh return a scrambled grid
verify:mom6_forge-a2.location: CrocoDash/visualCaseGen/external/mom6_forge/mom6_forge/utils.py:224-225 (consumers: mapping.py:52-56 grid_from_esmf_mesh, mapping.py:837-845 compute_smoothing_weights, mapping.py:316-317 write_mapping_file, utils.py:298-302 get_avg_resolution_km, _supergrid.py:844 reconstruct_from_esmf_mesh)
verify:mom6_forge-a2.what:
get_mesh_dimensions first gets nx exactly from element connectivity: nx is the index of the first element that shares an edge with element 0, which is the row stride. It then swaps nx and ny whenever mod(lon[nx//2]-lon[0], 360) < |lat[nx//2]-lat[0]| along the first row. Every caller reshapes the flat mesh arrays in C order as (ny, nx), so after the swap the 2D layout is scrambled. Not just transposed: consecutive elements of one true row are wrapped onto several short rows. Effects:
- grid_from_esmf_mesh returns a scrambled mask/lon/lat.
- extract_coastline_mask flags interior ocean cells as coast, so generate_ESMF_map_via_xesmf sends runoff to them.
- compute_smoothing_weights builds left/right/top/bottom neighbours from the wrong stride.
- get_avg_resolution_km returns a tiny value, so get_suggested_smoothing_params suggests rmax=1 km, fold=2 km instead of 20/40 km. CrocoDash RunoffConfigurator.configure uses this when rmax is not given, so smoothing is effectively turned off.
- write_mapping_file writes swapped nj_b/ni_b.
- Grid.from_esmf_mesh and Topo.from_esmf_mesh (via reconstruct_from_esmf_mesh) return a grid with the wrong shape and wrong coordinates.
No error is raised.
verify:mom6_forge-a2.trigger:
Any mom6_forge-written ocean mesh with nx != ny whose first grid row runs more north-south than eastward in degree space. Two ways to get one:
- Grid.from_center(..., angle_deg=A) with roughly atan(1/cos(lat)) < |A| < 90. That is |A| above about 49° at 30N; 60 and -60 both trigger. Rows that run westward (|A| > 90, e.g. 120) do not trigger, because of the mod 360.
- Grid.from_projection("EPSG:3995", ...) domains offset along the projection x axis, e.g. x in [1500, 2500] km or [-2500, -1500] km.
User paths:
- A CrocoDash Case with a DROF compset (RunoffConfigurator is required for DROF): configure_forcings computes the rmax/fold suggestion and process_forcings calls gen_rof_maps.
- The visualCaseGen runoff_mapping_generator GUI.
- Grid.from_esmf_mesh / Topo.from_esmf_mesh on such a mesh.

verify:mom6_forge-a2.root_cause: A lon/lat orientation heuristic (utils.py:220-225) overrides the exact, connectivity-derived nx. That nx is always the fast-varying stride that all callers' reshape(ny, nx) and row-neighbour arithmetic depend on. On rotated or offset-projection grids the rows are not zonal, so the heuristic fires and the counts no longer match the storage order. The swap is also inconsistent for a genuinely column-major mesh: there, swapping the counts without transposing the data scrambles the reshape too. So the swap is never what the reshape consumers need.
verify:mom6_forge-a2.smallest_fix: Remove the swap in get_mesh_dimensions (utils.py:214-225) and return the connectivity-derived (nx, len//nx). The narrowest version: skip the swap when the mesh has the "grid_topology" attr that to_esmf_mesh always writes, since mom6_forge meshes are always row-major. The repro's monkeypatch does this and restores coast-only runoff mapping. If orientation ever matters for a foreign column-major mesh, transpose the reshaped arrays in grid_from_esmf_mesh/flatten_to_mesh instead of swapping the counts. A follow-up for get_avg_resolution_km: compute great-circle dx/dy rather than dlon*cos(lat)/dlat, which is also wrong on rotated grids.
verify:mom6_forge-a2.fixed_on_main: No. mom6_forge origin/main 83d7692 (also checked on GitHub NCAR/mom6_forge main) still has the swap, at utils.py:226-227. Neither #126 nor #155 touches it. A pin bump would not fix it.

findings.title: CESM POP IC/OBC velocities are used as east/north values on T-points, but POP's UVEL/VVEL are grid-relative and sit on U-points
findings.what: CESM_POP_OUTPUT gives UVEL/VVEL the coordinates TLAT/TLONG (an A-grid). Nothing in the GET step or the regrid step rotates them by POP's ANGLE. regional-mom6 then treats them as earth-relative (east/north) values and only rotates them onto the MOM6 grid. POP's own metadata says UVEL is 'Velocity in grid-x direction' with coordinates 'ULONG ULAT'. So every POP-sourced IC and OBC velocity is rotated wrongly by the local POP grid angle, and is also placed half a POP cell (about 0.03-0.05 degrees on HR) away from where it belongs.
findings.trigger: Any case with product_name='cesm_pop_output' (CESM-HR FOSI or LENS2) whose domain lies where POP's grid is not aligned east/north. On the HR tripole grid that is north of about 30N; LENS2's displaced-pole gx1v7 grid is rotated across most of the NH (not measured here). It applies to process_forcings for both the IC and the OBCs.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/rm6/pop_rot.py. It builds a POP-like source with grid-relative UVEL=100 cm/s, VVEL=0 and ANGLE=30deg, then runs CrocoDash's _regrid_obc_chunk with CESM_POP_OUTPUT.write_metadata() on an unrotated MOM6 grid. Expected u=0.866, v=0.5 m/s. Observed u=1.0, v=0.0 at every segment point. Real data: in the HR UVEL file (.../FOSI_BGC/HR/.../month_1/...pop.h.UVEL.195801-195812.nc), |ANGLE| has median 2.2 and max 7.3 deg at 30-45N, median 7.7 and max 27.5 deg at 45-60N, and median 29 and max 82 deg at 60-75N. It is exactly 0 south of 30N. grep finds no use of ANGLE, ULAT or ULONG anywhere in CrocoDash/raw_data_access or CrocoDash/forcing.
findings.root_cause: The product definition assumes an A-grid with earth-relative velocities. identify_arakawa_grid sees nlon/nlat for every variable, returns 'A', and reuses the T-point tracer regridder for u and v. No step turns POP's grid-relative B-grid velocities into earth-relative ones.
findings.smallest_fix: In the CESM-POP GET step (read_single_variable_tseries_data, or a post-read hook for CESM_POP_OUTPUT), rotate to east/north with u_e = UVEL*cos(ANGLE) - VVEL*sin(ANGLE) and v_n = UVEL*sin(ANGLE) + VVEL*cos(ANGLE), where ANGLE is at U-points. Then average the result to T-points (4-point mean) so the declared A-grid is true, or carry ULONG/ULAT and declare a B-grid that the regridders honour. Do this after TRIAGE item 1 (#353), which currently stops many POP cases earlier.

findings.title: Tidal OBCs are zeroed or filled from neighbours on boundaries near 0 deg longitude: TPXO regridders are non-periodic and TPXO is (nx, ny)-ordered
findings.what: Segment.regrid_tides builds its three xESMF regridders from the global TPXO field with periodic=False. TPXO9.v1's longitudes run 0.083-359.917 for u, 0.167-360.0 for h and 0.167-... for v, so segment points within about 1/6 deg of 0 deg longitude are unmapped and come back NaN. ap2ep mixes u and v, so a NaN in either makes uamp, vamp, uphase and vphase all NaN. With no mask (CrocoDash passes no bathymetry), encode_tidal_files_and_output then fills every NaN with 0. An east or west boundary inside that band therefore gets zero tidal velocity, or zero tidal elevation for the h gap, along its whole length, and the only sign is a generic warning. A north or south boundary crossing 0 deg has its points in the band silently filled from neighbours.
findings.trigger: configure_forcings(..., tpxo_elevation_filepath, tpxo_velocity_filepath, tidal_constituents) followed by process_forcings on a grid with an open boundary whose longitude lies in (359.92, 0.17) mod 360, e.g. Grid(xstart=0.0, ...), or a boundary crossing the prime meridian.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/rm6/tides_seam.py (real TPXO9.v1 files, M2 only, open ocean at lat -4..-2). With `python tides_seam.py tides/x0.0 0.0 -4.0` the west segment at lon 0.0 gives uamp = vamp = 0 at 17/17 points while zamp is 0.43 m. The east segment at lon 2.0 gives uamp 0.014 and vamp 0.010. With xstart=1.0 the same west boundary gives uamp 0.015. The candidate fix in tides_seam_fix.py (TPXO transposed to (constituent, ny, nx) plus periodic=True) gives west uamp 0.0170 and vamp 0.0102 at xstart=0, and leaves the xstart=1 outputs bit-identical.
findings.root_cause: There is no periodicity across TPXO's 0/360 seam: create_regridder's default is periodic=False and regrid_tides never sets it. Passing periodic=True alone is not enough, because TPXO's lon/lat are dimensioned (nx, ny) and xESMF treats the last horizontal dim as the periodic x axis. This is the remaining form of regional-mom6 #15: the slicing problem in that issue is gone, but the seam gap is still there. TRIAGE B proposes closing #15 as likely fixed, and this repro shows it is not.
findings.smallest_fix: In prepare_tpxo_tidal_forcing, transpose each TPXO dataset to (constituent, ny, nx). In regrid_tides, pass periodic=True to the three rgd.create_regridder calls. Both were verified by monkeypatch in tides_seam_fix.py. Optionally, raise instead of zero-filling when a whole tidal segment is NaN.

findings.title: Tides configurator always sets TIDE_M2=True and never sets the selected constituents' TIDE_* flags
findings.what: TidesConfigurator.configure writes TIDE_M2 = True unconditionally, and writes no TIDE_<X> for the other constituents in tidal_constituents. In MOM6 every TIDE_<X> defaults to False (MOM_tidal_forcing.F90:298-318). So with TIDES=True the astronomical body-tide forcing always contains M2 and only M2, whatever constituents the OBCs carry. A K1/O1-only case therefore gets M2 body forcing with no M2 at the boundaries, and an M2+S2+K1+O1 case gets body forcing for M2 alone.
findings.trigger: configure_forcings with tidal_constituents set to anything other than ['M2'], e.g. ['K1','O1'] or ['M2','S2','K1','O1'].
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/rm6/tides_cfg.py (case audit_rm6_tide2, tidal_constituents=['K1','O1']). The resulting user_nl_mom contains 'TIDES = True', 'TIDE_M2 = True', 'OBC_TIDE_CONSTITUENTS = "K1, O1"' and no TIDE_K1 or TIDE_O1. MOM6 defaults were checked in ~/work/installs/CESM_crocodash/components/mom/MOM6/src/parameterizations/lateral/MOM_tidal_forcing.F90:298-318 (all default=.false.).
findings.root_cause: Hard-coded output param; the constituent list is only used for OBC_TIDE_*.
findings.smallest_fix: Write TIDE_<c> = True for each c in tidal_constituents, as dynamic UserNLConfigParams the way ConditionsConfigurator handles its per-boundary params, and drop the hard-coded TIDE_M2. Possibly related to the empty CrocoDash #344 ('OBC Tide Params are Changing!').

findings.title: crocodash duplicate crashes with IsADirectoryError on any case with tides, because the tides step leaves regional-mom6 experiment directories and a symlink cycle in inputdir/ocn
findings.what: TidesConfigurator.process builds a full rm6 experiment just to call setup_boundary_tides, with mom_run_dir=inputdir and mom_input_dir=inputdir/ocn. The constructor creates inputdir/ocn/weights/, inputdir/ocn/forcing/ and inputdir/ocn/hgrid.nc. It also creates two symlinks, inputdir/inputdir -> inputdir/ocn and inputdir/ocn/rundir -> inputdir, which together form a cycle. duplicate_case then runs shutil.copy on every entry of inputdir/ocn and dies on the first directory. That leaves a half-copied new case and inputdir. Any tool that follows symlinks (cp -rL, rsync -L, find -L, copytree) also loops on the cycle.
findings.trigger: process_forcings on a case configured with tides, then `crocodash duplicate` or CaseBundle/shareable.duplicate_case.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/rm6/tides_case.py (case audit_rm6_tide1, reference_ocean plus TPXO M2) creates ocn/weights, ocn/forcing, ocn/hgrid.nc, the symlink ocn/rundir -> inputdir and the symlink inputdir/inputdir -> inputdir/ocn. tides_dup.py then runs duplicate_case(...tide1, ...tide1dup, ...) and fails with IsADirectoryError: [Errno 21] Is a directory: '.../input/audit_rm6_tide1/ocn/weights' at shareable.py:415, with 9 files already copied into the new ocn. MOM_RPS was added to sys.path only to get past the known param_file_reader environment artifact.

findings.smallest_fix: In tides.py, call regional_mom6.prepare_tpxo_tidal_forcing plus Segment.cardinal(hgrid, b, f'segment_{n:03d}').regrid_tides(...) directly instead of constructing an experiment. In duplicate_case, copy only regular files (`if src.is_file() and not src.is_symlink()`). Related 1.1 items: #340 and #342 replace shareable.py.

findings.title: MOM_parameter_tools: deleting a parameter crashes when it has no comment, and removes other parameters whose lines contain its name and value
findings.what: write_MOM_file removes a deleted key by dropping every line that contains the key, its value and its comment as substrings. With no comment, the comment is None, so `None in line` raises TypeError and nothing is written. With a comment, the substring match also deletes unrelated parameters: deleting DT (1800) also deleted DT_THERM = 18000.
findings.trigger: change_MOM_parameter(rundir, name, delete=True) on a MOM_override, e.g. from rm6's own setup_generic/setup_rOM3 workflows or user scripts. This is not on CrocoDash's path; CrocoDash never imports MOM_parameter_tools.
findings.repro: /glade/derecho/scratch/manishrv/tmp/claude-44953/-glade-u-home-manishrv-documents-croc/8dbab665-7998-4a92-b4e6-579de0e188a7/scratchpad/audit/rm6/mpt_delete.py. With '#override DT = 1800' and no comment: TypeError: 'in <string>' requires string as left operand, not NoneType (MOM_parameter_tools.py:206). With '#override DT = 1800 ! set by user' and '#override DT_THERM = 18000 ! set by user', deleting DT leaves the file as '' (both lines removed).
findings.root_cause: Line removal uses substring containment instead of parsing each line's key, and does not handle comment=None.
findings.smallest_fix: While writing, parse each line's key (split on '=', strip '#override') and drop only the lines whose key equals the deleted key.

verify:creation_cli-a6.verdict_reason: I reproduced it with my own minimal script, using the real duplicate_case flow on a tiny NYF case with reference_ocean forcing. Nothing guards against it. apply_xmlchanges_to_case (shareable.py:94-105) splits each replay.sh line once on whitespace and once on '=', so everything after the '=' becomes the value, including the trailing ' --non-local'. CIME requires --non-local on every xmlchange a Casper user makes to a derecho case, and CrocoDash itself adds it when is_non_local is True. So every user change recorded in such a case's replay.sh carries the flag. It is not a known duplicate: no TRIAGE item or open issue covers it. The 1.1 items #340 (Q13) and #342 (Q15) replace this code with case_state.parse_xmlchanges, which uses shlex and handles flags, but 1.0.x users still hit the bug through `crocodash duplicate`, `crocodash fork` and the MCP duplicate/fork tools. One correction to the finding: the bug is not only a crash. String-typed variables are silently stored with ' --non-local' appended (seen for DOUT_S_ROOT), which is a wrong result.
verify:creation_cli-a6.title: duplicate_case and fork replay './xmlchange VAR=VAL --non-local' with '--non-local' kept in the value: logical and integer variables crash after the new case is created, string variables are silently set to 'VAL --non-local'
verify:creation_cli-a6.location: CrocoDash/shareable.py:101-105 (apply_xmlchanges_to_case); same parsing in CrocoDash/shareable.py:192-196 (CaseBundle._read_xmlchanges); called from CrocoDash/shareable.py:436 (duplicate_case) and CrocoDash/shareable.py:709 (ForkBundle.apply_copy_plan)
verify:creation_cli-a6.what:
To carry user xmlchanges over to a new case, apply_xmlchanges_to_case re-reads the source replay.sh. It parses each line with `_, kv = line.split(None, 1); param, value = kv.split("=", 1)` and calls xmlchange(param, value, is_non_local=True). For the line `./xmlchange DOUT_S=FALSE --non-local` this gives value 'FALSE --non-local', and the command run is `./xmlchange 'DOUT_S=FALSE --non-local' --non-local`.
- **Logical or integer variable:** CIME rejects the value and the RuntimeError propagates out of duplicate_case. By then the new caseroot and inputdir already exist, with its xml files, user_nl and SourceMods already copied. Changes listed later in replay.sh are not applied, and the optional bundle step is skipped.
- **String variable** (DOUT_S_ROOT, for example): CIME accepts 'VAL --non-local' and the new case silently gets a corrupted value.
- **Fork:** ForkBundle.fork with plan xmlchanges=true runs the same function on the bundle's replay.sh.
verify:creation_cli-a6.trigger: Any case whose user xmlchanges were made with a flag. The common case is a derecho case created or edited from Casper (NCAR JupyterHub). There CIME refuses a plain ./xmlchange ('Current machine casper does not match case machine derecho') and CrocoDash's own is_non_local is True, so every replay.sh line ends in --non-local. When the user has changed a variable that CrocoDash itself does not set (DOUT_S, DOUT_S_ROOT, JOB_PRIORITY, ...), it is flagged as non-standard and replayed by `crocodash duplicate`, by Case/CaseBundle.duplicate_case, or by `crocodash fork` with plan xmlchanges=true. Leading flags break it too. `./xmlchange --force DOUT_S=FALSE` produces the key '--force DOUT_S', which argparse then rejects. The `--id X --val Y` form has no '=' and is silently dropped.

verify:creation_cli-a7.what: CaseBundle.diff() checks only whether a user_nl parameter name or xmlchange variable name exists in the freshly created reference case. It never compares values. Any parameter the reference case also writes therefore counts as "standard", even when the user changed its value. For user_nl_mom that includes DT, DT_THERM, MINIMUM_DEPTH/MAXIMUM_DEPTH, the OBC_* settings and the OBC_SEGMENT_*_VELOCITY_NUDGING_TIMESCALES. That is 1 or more whenever the domain has any ocean point, so `if nodes_needed < 1: return None` only runs for an all-land domain. Every domain with 1 to 21,760 ocean points (non-MARBL, Derecho) gets --pecount S. MOM_interface's S tier puts NTASKS_OCN=128 on a dedicated node (ROOTPE_OCN=128) and 128 ATM/CPL/ROF tasks on node 0, so the job takes 2 nodes and 256 tasks. The 1-task XS tier is never requested, although PR #233's description says the code picks among XS/S/M/L. The docstring's fallback is no better: returning None leaves CIME's create_newcase default of pecount M, which gives 384 OCN tasks. When the grid has fewer than 128 columns, MOM6 has a check that is expected to abort the run at init ("You requested to use 128 PEs but there are only N columns in the model"). Larger small domains run, but they waste a node and cannot use small queues.

verify:configure_process-a1.title: BGC river nutrients: DON and SiO3 fluxes come out 100x too small, DOP and Fe 100x too large
verify:configure_process-a1.what:
BGCRiverNutrientsConfigurator.process scales the river fluxes by 0.01 to convert nmol/cm^2/s to mmol/m^2/s. Its list of variables to convert names don_riv_flux and dsi_riv_flux twice and leaves out dop_riv_flux and dfe_riv_flux. As a result:

verify:configure_process-a3.title: STOP_N counts Gregorian days for NO_LEAP (CESM output) products, so the run goes past its last OBC record when the dates span Feb 29
verify:configure_process-a3.what: configure_forcings sets CALENDAR from the forcing product. That is NO_LEAP for CESM_POP_OUTPUT and CESM_MOM_OUTPUT. It then sets STOP_OPTION=ndays and STOP_N=(date_range[1] - date_range[0]).days, which pandas counts on the proleptic Gregorian calendar. Every Feb 29 inside date_range adds a day that the NO_LEAP model does not have, so the model stops k days after date_range[1] (k = number of leap days in the range). The OBC files that process_forcings writes cover exactly [date_range[0], date_range[1]] in the noleap calendar, with no modulo attribute. Once model time passes the last record, FMS time_interp_external has no record to interpolate to and stops the run with a FATAL error. If the data did reach further, the run would still be k days longer than the user asked for.

verify:configure_process-a8.root_cause: TidesConfigurator relies on BaseConfigurator.validate_args (base.py:665), which only checks that the expected argument names are present and no extra ones are given. verify:configure_process-a8.smallest_fix: Override validate_args in TidesConfigurator: call super().validate_args(**kwargs), then require tidal_constituents to be a non-empty list or tuple of str. Also check each name against the TPXO-supported set (M2, S2, N2, K2, K1, O1, P1, Q1, MM, MF) and raise ValueError on unknown ones, so the error comes at configure time. Keep in mind that BaseConfigurator.inspect() builds configurators with "" placeholders, so the check must allow that path, or inspect must skip it.

verify:raw_data-a5.what: get_global_data_with_python sends "download_format": "zip" but passes client.retrieve a target of Path(output_folder)/output_filename (default glofas_data.nc) and returns that path. The client writes the server's payload unchanged, so the returned ".nc" is a zip archive, and xr.open_dataset on it fails with xarray's generic "did not find a match in any of xarray's currently installed IO backends". The dates are expanded with pd.date_range and then reduced to three independent sorted sets (hyear, hmonth, hday). CDS/EWDS take the Cartesian product of these, so any window that crosses a month or year boundary pulls in days outside [start, end]. The docstring says "every day in the range is requested", which hides this. Examples: 2019-12-30..2020-01-02 (4 days) selects 16 days, including Jan 2019 and Dec 2020. 2020-01-30..02-02 (4 days) selects 6. 2020-01-15..03-15 (61 days) selects 91. A June-to-May year selects about 2 full years.

verify:raw_data-a2.verdict_reason: I reproduced this end to end through the public API. A tiny Case was configured with product_name='CESM_MOM_OUTPUT' and function_name='get_mom6_output_data', with dataset_path pointing at synthetic native-MOM6 daily output from a GREGORIAN parent. configure_forcings ran './xmlchange CALENDAR=NO_LEAP', and process_forcings then crashed in the OBC regrid with "ValueError: invalid day number provided in cftime.DatetimeNoLeap(2020, 2, 29, 12, ...)". Two controls on the same data: a window without Feb 29 regrids fine, and the Feb 27 to Mar 2 window regrids fine once the product calendar is swapped for GREGORIAN. Nothing in TRIAGE.md, the open issue and PR lists, or QUEUE.md covers it. Open PR #327 and issues #333, #335, #345 and #347 have no calendar fix for this product, and Q5 only makes slicing work in the data's own calendar. rm6 is behaving correctly: it encodes in the calendar CrocoDash gives it. So the bug is CrocoDash's, not regional-mom6's.

The product metadata written to config.json also carries calendar noleap, and the OBC regrid uses it to encode the segment times, whatever calendar the parent actually ran. Any CrocoDash case forced by GLORYS, the reference products, ERA5 and so on runs GREGORIAN. That includes the parent in the gallery nesting demo. When such a run is the parent, its output holds real Feb 29 records. Any child window that contains Feb 29 of a leap year then crashes in the OBC regrid with a cftime 'invalid day number' error that does not name the cause. Windows without Feb 29 work, but the child silently runs NO_LEAP while its parent runs GREGORIAN.

verify:configure_process-a5.what: The resume checks in the forcing pipeline treat 'the file exists and its first 4 bytes are a netCDF/HDF5 signature' as 'this step finished'. That covers fetch_raw_chunk (raw OBC chunks and ic_unprocessed.nc), _merge_boundary (ocn/forcing_obc_segment_NNN.nc), _regrid_ic via _all_written (init_*.nc and init_*_filled.nc) and the BGC per-tracer split files. All of these are written in place under their final names: by the product's access function (e.g. glorys.py:106, reference.py:202), at obc.py:690, by rm6's setup_initial_condition, at mom6.py:278 and at mom6.py:224. With netCDF4 the header and all metadata are on disk before the data. A write that is interrupted therefore leaves a file that passes the check and even opens cleanly, but every value reads back as the fill value (NaN). On the next process_forcings run it is skipped and used as if complete. A truncated raw chunk is regridded to a boundary of zeros (T=0, S=0, u=v=eta=0). A truncated merged OBC file or IC file is kept as all-NaN. In both cases process_forcings exits 0. The failure surfaces only when MOM6 runs, or the run silently uses wrong forcing. If the kill lands before the metadata is flushed, the rerun instead dies in REGRID with 'NetCDF: HDF error: <path>'. The REGRID step (obc.py:368-418) and BGC split step 3 already write to a scratch name and os.replace it, so they are not affected. BGC split step 2 (the per-tracer files) is affected; the finder said the BGC split was already safe, which holds only for step 3. The _all_written docstring assumes 'a run killed partway leaves only some of them', which is false for the file being written.
verify:configure_process-a5.trigger: process_forcings / crocodash process is interrupted while it writes a raw chunk, a merged OBC file, an IC file or a BGC per-tracer file. Causes include a PBS walltime kill, the OOM killer, Ctrl-C or a kernel interrupt, or an exception mid-write such as a disk-quota error or a source read error during the lazy GLORYS RDA write. The user then reruns process_forcings to resume, as the docs advertise (3b_process_forcings.md: 'Resume a partially-completed run'; obc.py docstring: 'Re-running after a partial failure resumes from the last completed file'). The GLORYS RDA GET write (glorys.py:106) streams lazily from campaign storage and the merge write streams from open_mfdataset. These are long writes on big domains, so they are the likeliest places for a kill to land.

verify:configure_process-a5.root_cause: The skip checks are existence plus a magic-byte check, which says nothing about completeness. The outputs are written directly to their final names instead of to a temp name renamed into place when done. HDF5/netCDF4 puts the signature and metadata on disk first, so a partial file passes the check and even opens cleanly, reading back as fill values. Downstream NaN filling then turns a NaN raw chunk into a boundary of zeros.
verify:configure_process-a5.smallest_fix: Write each of these outputs to a temp name in the same directory and os.replace it into place only after the write returns. REGRID (obc.py:418) and BGC step 3 (mom6.py:247-249) already do this. (1) fetch_raw_chunk: for in-process access functions (data_access_fn._type == "python"), pass output_filename=f"{name}.part", then os.replace(part, output_file) and remove any leftover .part first. Keep the final name for type="script" functions, whose download runs later. (2) _merge_boundary: to_netcdf to output_path + ".tmp", then os.replace. (3) _fill_missing_and_write: the same. (4) _regrid_ic: run setup_initial_condition with expt.mom_input_dir set to a temp subdirectory and move the three init_*.nc files into output_dir afterwards. (5) BGC split step 2: the same tmp + replace. The finder's optional fix, validating by opening the file, would NOT catch this: the killed files open fine and read as NaN.
verify:configure_process-a5.fixed_on_main: No (target is main). No open PR fixes it. #336 / Q10 (branch finished-steps, 9eeb7400) also leaves it open. Its clean() deletes a step's files only when that step already has a finished_steps.json entry. A step killed before finishing has no entry, so its partial files are kept even with --force.

verify:raw_data-a1.what: POP's UVEL/VVEL are components along the POP grid's own axes. Both FOSI and LENS2 files give long_name "Velocity in grid-x direction", and each file includes ANGLE (radians, at U points). CESM_POP_OUTPUT hands them to regional-mom6 as u_var_name/v_var_name. regional-mom6 assumes these are earth-relative and rotates only by the target grid's angle_dx. The source ANGLE gets copied into the raw *_unprocessed.nc and ic_unprocessed.nc files, but nothing reads it. As a result, initial-condition and open-boundary velocities point the wrong way, rotated by the POP grid angle at that location. Nothing warns about it. A secondary problem: u/v lat/lon metadata point at TLAT/TLONG, so the pipeline detects an Arakawa A grid and regrids UVEL/VVEL as if they sat at T points. They actually sit at U points, the NE cell corner, which is half a cell away.

verify:rm6-a5.title: change_MOM_parameter(delete=True) crashes on uncommented parameters, deletes other parameters, and rewrites plain ones as '= None'
verify:rm6-a5.what: write_MOM_file removes a deleted key by dropping every line that contains the key name, its old value and its old comment as substrings (all(word in line for word in [key, value, comment])). There are three failures. (1) When the parameter has no '!' comment, comment is None. Any line that contains the key and its value then evaluates `None in line`, which raises TypeError, and nothing is written. This hits rm6's own shipped demo MOM_override, whose lines have no comments, and every parameter that change_MOM_parameter or setup_generic adds with the default comment=None. (2) When there is a comment, the substring match also removes unrelated parameters: deleting DT = 1800 also deletes DT_THERM = 18000 if the comments match. (3) Deleting a plain (non-#override) line in MOM_override does not remove it. Line 126 indexes MOM_file_dict[var] on a defaultdict, which re-creates the deleted key with value None, so the line is rewritten as '#override FOO = None ! Modified by regional-mom6. Was 1'.
