verify:mom6_forge-a7.title: Cressman fallback fill (iterative_fill) turns unfilled coastal ocean cells into NaN, which the TOPO_FILE writes as min_depth+0.1
verify:mom6_forge-a7.location: CrocoDash/visualCaseGen/external/mom6_forge/mom6_forge/utils.py:488-505 (filled_f at 488, unweighted d_nbr at 493-495); NaN input comes from CrocoDash/visualCaseGen/external/mom6_forge/mom6_forge/topo.py:1653 (dst_ds["mask"] = self.tmask) via mapping.py regrid_dataset_via_xesmf; NaN is turned into min_depth+0.1 at topo.py:382-391 (masked_depth)
verify:mom6_forge-a7.what:
direct_cressman_interp regrids with xESMF onto a dst_ds that contains a "mask" variable. xESMF therefore sets unmapped_to_nan=True (xesmf/frontend.py, any version >= 0.8), so every land cell and every "unfilled" ocean cell (no source ocean point within L) is NaN in the Cressman output. The docstring of regrid_dataset_via_cressman (mapping.py:1695) says unfilled cells are 0, which is wrong.

iterative_fill makes this worse in two ways:
- It counts every land cell as a donor: filled_f = ~unfilled_2d.
- It builds the numerator d_nbr from the raw depth of all four neighbours, not just the donors.

As a result, any unfilled cell that has a land neighbour or a still-unfilled neighbour is "filled" with NaN on the first pass. NaN then spreads to the remaining unfilled cells on later passes. Topo.masked_depth turns NaN ocean cells into min_depth+0.1 (NaN > min_depth is False), and write_topo writes that value into the MOM6 TOPO_FILE "depth" variable, while depth_raw stays NaN.

So the fallback almost never produces a neighbour average. The cells it should fill silently become min_depth+0.1-deep shelves. With land at 0 (iterative_fill called directly), the land-donor bias the finder described also exists, giving 50 m instead of 100 m.
verify:mom6_forge-a7.trigger:
Topo.set_from_dataset with depth_method="cressman", or with the automatic Cressman choice (resolution ratio >= 12x), or a direct topo.direct_cressman_interp() call, where the active mask marks as ocean a cell that has no source ocean point (depth > 0) within L = smooth_scl*sqrt(tarea). Typical cases:
- a mask_method="naturalearth" coastline that disagrees with the source dataset;
- a manual or TopoEditor mask edit that opens water, after which Cressman is rerun (the set_from_dataset warning tells users to do this).

Reachable from CrocoDash YAML/CLI as well, because recipe.build_topo passes topo.source kwargs straight to set_from_dataset (CrocoDash/recipe.py:109).

verify:mom6_forge-a7.root_cause:
iterative_fill does not restrict its donors to finite, filled ocean cells:
- filled_f = (~unfilled_2d) counts land as filled.
- d_nbr sums np.pad(depth, mode="edge") over all four neighbours without weighting by filled_f, so land cells and still-unfilled cells feed the numerator.

In the Cressman pipeline those cells are NaN, because dst_ds has a "mask" variable and xESMF therefore maps unmapped cells to NaN. Every fill touching land or another unfilled cell becomes NaN, and Topo.masked_depth then turns it into min_depth+0.1.
verify:mom6_forge-a7.smallest_fix:
In iterative_fill, compute on each pass:

```python
donor = (~unfilled_2d) & mask_2d & np.isfinite(depth)  # mask_2d = all True when mask is None
d_pad = np.pad(np.where(donor, depth, 0.0), 1)
f_pad = np.pad(donor.astype(float), 1)
```

Then use d_nbr / f_nbr as now. Verified by monkeypatch: column 7 becomes 100 m.

Masking filled_f alone (the finder's fix) is not enough, because the numerator still sums NaN. Optionally also correct the "Unfilled ocean cells are 0" docstring at mapping.py:1695.

verify:rm6-a2.title: Tidal OBCs come out as zero on an east/west boundary within 1/6 deg of 0 deg longitude: TPXO regridders are non-periodic and TPXO is (nx, ny)-ordered
verify:rm6-a2.location: CrocoDash/rm6/regional_mom6/segment.py:1147 (also 1155, 1163: the three rgd.create_regridder calls in Segment.regrid_tides, all without periodic); CrocoDash/rm6/regional_mom6/regional_mom6.py:122-151 (prepare_tpxo_tidal_forcing leaves TPXO in (nc, nx, ny) order); CrocoDash/rm6/regional_mom6/regridding.py:109 (periodic=False default) and :522 (fillna(0) when segment.mask is None); reached from CrocoDash/forcing/tides.py:143
verify:rm6-a2.what:
Segment.regrid_tides builds its elevation, u and v xESMF regridders from the global TPXO fields with periodic=False, and create_regridder sets unmapped_to_nan=True. The TPXO9.v1 longitude ranges are: h (lon_z) 0.1667..360.0, u (lon_u) 0.0833..359.9167, v (lon_v) 0.1667..360.0. Each grid therefore has a 1/6 deg gap at the 0/360 seam, and segment points inside a gap come back NaN. fill_missing_data only ffills/bfills along the segment, so an east or west segment entirely inside a gap stays all-NaN. ap2ep mixes u and v, so a NaN in either one makes uamp, vamp, uphase and vphase all NaN. CrocoDash passes no bathymetry, so mask_dataset then replaces every NaN with 0. Results:
- East/west boundary at a lon in (359.917, 0.167): zero tidal velocity along its whole length.
- East/west boundary at a lon in (0, 0.167): zero tidal elevation too.
- Exactly lon 0.0: velocities zero, elevation fine.
The only message is "All NaNs filled b/c no ocean/land mask was available", and it is printed for every boundary, healthy ones included, so it gives no signal. North/south boundaries crossing 0 deg get the gap points copied from the nearest mapped neighbour. That error is small: up to ~0.016 m on a 0.3 m-varying field.
verify:rm6-a2.trigger: Any CrocoDash case with tides (configure_forcings(..., tpxo_elevation_filepath=..., tpxo_velocity_filepath=..., tidal_constituents=[...]) then process_forcings) whose west or east open boundary lies within about 1/6 deg of the prime meridian. Examples: Grid(xstart=0.0, ...), xstart=0.1, or a domain whose east edge ends at 0 deg. Longitude convention does not matter: -0.05 and 359.95 behave the same.

verify:rm6-a2.root_cause: The tidal regridders have no periodicity across TPXO's 0/360 seam. create_regridder defaults to periodic=False and regrid_tides never overrides it, so ESMF leaves points between the last and first TPXO columns unmapped (NaN). Two downstream steps turn this into zeros. First, fill_missing_data can only fill along the segment, so a north/south-running (east/west) segment that sits entirely in the gap stays all-NaN. Second, mask_dataset with no mask fills NaN with 0 (CrocoDash/forcing/tides.py never passes bathymetry_path). Passing periodic=True alone does not help: prepare_tpxo_tidal_forcing keeps TPXO's native (nx, ny) ordering, and xESMF assumes the last horizontal dim is x and makes the ESMF dim built from it periodic, i.e. latitude here (verified: periodic-only output is identical to pinned). This is the remaining form of regional-mom6 #15. The slicing problem that issue describes is gone, but the seam gap remains.

verify:vcg-a7.title: configure_forcings() on an earlier case raises a bare TypeError/KeyError instead of the guard's RuntimeError after a later Case() call fails
verify:vcg-a7.what:
The multi-case guard in Case.configure_forcings (case.py:623, `active_caseroot = Path(cvars["CASEROOT"].value)`) assumes visualCaseGen's global cvars always holds a CASEROOT string. Case.__init__ resets that global state first: initialize_visualCaseGen(cesmroot) at case.py:138 runs ConfigVar.reboot (visualCaseGen/initialize.py:31), which pops every cvar. It does this before Case.init_args_check (case.py:147) and before _configure_launch sets CASEROOT (case.py:1060). So when a second Case() fails, it leaves CASEROOT in one of two states:
- None, if the failure is in argument validation or in _configure_case before the launch stage.
- Missing entirely, if the failure is inside initialize_visualCaseGen, e.g. a bad cesmroot.

After that, configure_forcings() on the earlier, valid case crashes inside the guard with a bare `TypeError: expected str, bytes or os.PathLike object, not NoneType` or `KeyError: 'CASEROOT'`. The docstring promises a RuntimeError that explains the case can no longer be configured in this session. Rerunning configure_forcings on that case, which the docs say is supported, fails the same way.

2. Run another Case(...) cell with a typo, e.g. atm_grid_name="T63x" or a cesmroot that does not exist. It raises, as it should.
3. Go back and call A.configure_forcings(...) again, e.g. with a changed date_range.

verify:vcg-a4.root_cause: Python caches the CIME package in sys.modules on first import. Appending another cimeroot to sys.path (at the end, too) never re-imports it. CIME's get_cime_root(), get_config_path() and get_schema_path() derive every config path from the loaded module's __file__, so Files() and everything built on it describe the first tree. Nothing checks that the imported CIME is the one under self.cimeroot. CrocoDash creates a new CIME_interface per Case (case.py:138) on the assumption that this gives a clean per-cesmroot view, and it does not.
verify:vcg-a4.smallest_fix: In CIME_interface.__init__, after _set_cimeroot: if 'CIME' is in sys.modules and Path(sys.modules['CIME'].__file__).resolve().parent.parent != self.cimeroot.resolve(), raise RuntimeError("visualCaseGen already loaded CIME from <A> in this process; restart the kernel/process to use <B>"). Compare resolved paths: ~/work is a symlink to /glade/work, so unresolved paths differ even for the same tree. Append the root to sys.path only if it is not already there. This was verified by monkeypatch (fix_check.py). Purging and re-importing CIME is not recommended because CIME keeps module-level state.

skeptic:raw_data-a5.reason: I found nothing that refutes it. The method has no caller anywhere in CrocoDash: configure_forcings/process_forcings never use it, and the gallery only demonstrates the _script_for_cli variant. Nothing unzips the download or trims its dates, and the only test (tests/raw_data_access/test_glofas.py:16, slow) asserts os.path.exists and nothing more. It is still a public, registered access method that users can reach with ProductRegistry.get_access_function('glofas','get_global_data_with_python'). The verifier faked cdsapi.Client. I did not: my repro runs the real installed stack (cdsapi 0.7.7, which dispatches to ecmwf.datastores LegacyClient 0.5.3) over real HTTP against a stub of the EWDS retrieve API on 127.0.0.1. CrocoDash and the client libraries are not patched. The stub models only two server behaviours I cannot check offline. First, download_format='zip' returns a zip archive; this is the field's documented meaning, and the installed ecmwf-datastores README uses 'unarchived' to get a raw file. Second, hyear x hmonth x hday is taken as a Cartesian product, which is the standard CDS/EWDS form semantics. The client writes the asset bytes unchanged to the target named .nc (bytes on disk == server bytes: True), so the returned path is a zip that xarray cannot open. The request the audited code sends is captured verbatim, and its date sets cover more days than the window whenever the window crosses a month boundary. Monkeypatching download_format='unarchived' makes the returned file open. Caveat on that fix: EWDS may still zip a multi-file result even with 'unarchived', so extracting the zip or checking zipfile.is_zipfile is the safer fix. Clipping to [start, end] is still needed either way. Severity 'wrong result' is fair and not inflated: the function returns a non-netCDF file under a .nc name, with up to about 2x the requested days. It does not crash itself, and the path is off the main forcing workflow.

verify:vcg-a8.what: CrocoDash builds CaseCreator with add_grids_to_ccs_config=False (CrocoDash/case.py:480), so create_newcase runs with --res USER_RES. The USER_RES alias is empty, so the ATM and LND grids start as null (NX/NY=0) and the ROF grid gets the model_grid_defaults value for DROF, rx1 (360x180). _update_component_grids_xml then xmlchanges ATM_GRID, LND_GRID and ROF_GRID and their DOMAIN_MESH, but not their NX/NY. It does set NX/NY for OCN, ICE and WAV. The result for any DROF%GLOFAS compset is ROF_GRID=GLOFAS with the GLOFAS mesh (7200x3000 = 21.6M elements) but ROF_NX=360 and ROF_NY=180, plus ATM_NX/NY=0 and LND_NX/NY=0. GRID keeps the stale long name a%null_l%null_oi%null_r%rx1_.... DROF's namelist takes nx_global/ny_global from $ROF_NX/$ROF_NY (namelist_definition_drof.xml), and the generated drof_in has nx_global = 360 and ny_global = 180. DROF exports these to the mediator. med_phases_restart_write passes them to med_io_write, which only logs a 'grid2d size not consistent' warning, defines rofImp_nx=360 and rofImp_ny=180, and writes the rof import and fraction fields into those 64,800 slots. The cpl.r file therefore holds only the first 64,800 GLOFAS points (lat -59.975..-59.575) and drops the other 99.7%. On a continue run, med_io_read_init_iodesc reads with the file's 360x180 dims and only warns when ng > grid size, so it does not warn here. ATM_NX/NY=0 is harmless (the mediator falls back to a 1-D layout: atmImp_nx=204800, atmImp_ny=1). The run does not crash, and I found nothing showing the ocean solution changes. On a restart the truncated rofImp should reach only med_phases_diag_rof before DROF refreshes it; that is reasoned from nuopc.runseq, not run.

verify:vcg-a10.title: A grid named after a CESM grid (e.g. tx2_3v2) is refused with a false "previous case was deleted" reason, and the advised override=True builds a regional case on that global grid's MOM6 defaults
verify:vcg-a10.what: init_args_check refuses an ocn_grid whose name is in cime.domains["ocnice"] unless override=True (case.py:348-353). The message says this "happens when a previous case with this grid was deleted without using override=True" and tells the user to pass override=True. But CrocoDash creates cases with add_grids_to_ccs_config=False (case.py:479-481), so it never registers a grid in ccs_config. For a CrocoDash user, the check can only fire when the name matches one of CESM's own grids (tx2_3v2, tx2_3v3, tx0.25v1, tx1v1, gx1v7, gx3v7, ...), or a name left in ccs_config by pre-#252 CrocoDash or by the vCG GUI. The reason given is false, and the advice is harmful. With override=True the check is skipped and visualCaseGen runs `xmlchange OCN_GRID=<name>`. MOM_interface's MOM_input.yaml and input_data_list.yaml key their defaults on OCN_GRID, so the regional case silently gets the global grid's physics and file settings. CrocoDash's user_nl_mom only overrides grid/topo/vgrid, NIGLOBAL/NJGLOBAL, TRIPOLAR_N, DT, IC and OBC. Anyone who already passes override=True, as the tutorials do, gets no message at all.
verify:vcg-a10.trigger: Grid(..., name="tx2_3v2"), or any other standard ocnice grid name, then Case(...). With override=False you get the misleading refusal. With override=True, as the message advises or as tutorials pass by default, the case is created with OCN_GRID=tx2_3v2.

verify:vcg-a10.root_cause: The check and its message were written in e34cbac6 (#223, 2026-06-15). CrocoDash then registered each custom grid in ccs_config (add_grids_to_ccs_config=True), so a leftover registration from a deleted case was the usual way to hit it, and override=True was a fair way past. 0cf5efee (#252/#215, 2026-07-09) moved CrocoDash to add_grids_to_ccs_config=False: visualCaseGen now runs `xmlchange OCN_GRID=<name>` and never writes ccs_config. The check, its message and the override bypass were kept. As a result, the names it now catches are CESM's own grids, and bypassing it puts a global grid's name into OCN_GRID, which MOM_interface's param templates use to choose defaults.
